objectives: Compare aerobic respiration with anaerobic pathways.
Interpret evidence from living-material and yeast investigations.
Plan controls and explain limitations of respiration measurements.
paragraphs: Cellular respiration is a set of reactions that transfers energy from food into forms cells can use, including ATP. Energy is transferred rather than created. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen; its overall school word equation is glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water, with energy transferred. In eukaryotic cells many aerobic stages occur in mitochondria, although the first stage of glucose breakdown occurs in cytoplasm. Living plants respire as well as animals, during both day and night, because their cells continually need energy.

When oxygen supply is insufficient, some cells can obtain a smaller amount of usable energy through anaerobic pathways. In muscle cells, a school-level summary is glucose → lactate, with a smaller energy transfer than in aerobic respiration. Yeast can ferment sugars to ethanol and carbon dioxide when oxygen is unavailable. The products therefore depend on the organism and pathway; it is incorrect to give ethanol as the main anaerobic product of human muscle. Carbon dioxide from yeast can inflate dough, while heat in a warm environment affects both yeast activity and gas behaviour.

An investigation needs an observable response linked to respiration. In a teacher-led comparison, germinating seeds may release more carbon dioxide or warm more than a suitable non-living comparison sample. A control helps distinguish living activity from room-temperature changes or apparatus effects. In a yeast experiment, a known sugar supply, equal yeast quantity and controlled temperature permit comparisons. A gas volume measured over time can indicate gas production, but trapped air, leaks and dissolved gas affect results. A gas test may be needed to support the identity of the collected gas.

Neither bubbling nor carbon dioxide alone proves that respiration was anaerobic. Aerobic respiration can also produce carbon dioxide, and visible bubbles can include expanding trapped air. Oxygen conditions must be controlled and documented by an approved method if comparing aerobic and anaerobic processes. All cultures and chemical gas tests require school guidance; do not culture unknown microbes or seal a fermenting system without pressure relief. In a report, show raw data, calculate rates over stated intervals and explain controls, repeats and limitations before drawing a conclusion about living metabolism.
examples: A yeast mixture gives 24 mL of gas over 6 minutes under the prescribed conditions. Its mean measured rate is 24/6 = 4 mL per minute. This is a gas-production rate, not a direct measurement of total ATP production.

A flask of germinating seeds becomes 2 °C warmer while a matched control changes by 0 °C. This supports energy transfer as heat from living seed activity, provided insulation, starting temperatures and sample amounts were comparable.

Yeast with sugar produces carbon dioxide, but the flask also contains oxygen. The observation supports metabolic gas production but does not establish exclusively anaerobic conditions. A stronger investigation documents oxygen availability and uses appropriate controls.
lessons.summary: Cellular respiration is a set of reactions that transfers energy from food into forms cells can use, including ATP.

lessons.title: Gaseous exchange in leaves, stems and roots
objectives: Explain diffusion through stomata and other plant surfaces.
Distinguish respiration, photosynthesis and net gas exchange.
Predict the effects of light and waterlogged soil with stated conditions.
paragraphs: Plants exchange gases with their surroundings without mammalian lungs or a blood system. Gases move mainly by diffusion along concentration or partial-pressure gradients. In many leaves, stomata allow air to pass between outside air and internal air spaces. Thin moist surfaces of mesophyll cells allow gases to dissolve and diffuse into or out of cells. Guard cells regulate stomatal opening, connecting the supply of carbon dioxide for photosynthesis with the need to limit water loss. The pattern of stomata and opening differs among plants and conditions.

Other organs also need gases. Lenticels provide exchange routes in the outer tissues of many woody stems. Young stems and other thin surfaces can exchange gases across their outer layers, while roots obtain oxygen mainly from air spaces in well-aerated soil. Oxygen diffuses through moist root surfaces to respiring cells. Soil that remains waterlogged has much less effective gas supply because diffusion through water is much slower than through air. Root injury in waterlogged soil therefore involves oxygen availability as well as water abundance.

Every living plant cell respires, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide in aerobic respiration. Photosynthetic cells in sufficient light also take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen through photosynthesis. These processes occur simultaneously in a green leaf during daylight. Net exchange is their combined outcome, not evidence that one has stopped. When photosynthesis exceeds respiration, the leaf shows net carbon-dioxide uptake and oxygen release; in darkness, photosynthesis stops while respiration continues, giving net oxygen uptake and carbon-dioxide release.

At a compensation condition, photosynthetic carbon-dioxide uptake balances respiratory release, so little net carbon-dioxide exchange is detected even though both processes remain active. The balance changes with light, temperature, tissue condition and other limits on photosynthesis. Stomatal closure can reduce carbon-dioxide entry and water loss at the same time. A prediction should therefore state its conditions: bright light may favour net oxygen release in a healthy, adequately watered leaf, but bright light alone does not guarantee it if stomata are closed or another factor is limiting.
examples: A healthy leaf in suitable bright light produces 12 arbitrary units of oxygen by photosynthesis while respiration uses 4 units over the same interval. Net oxygen release is 12 − 4 = 8 units; respiration has not stopped.

At night a green plant continues to respire. With no light-driven photosynthesis, oxygen moves into its living tissues and carbon dioxide moves out overall. The same diffusion principles apply although the net direction differs from a productive daylight leaf.

A pot is kept permanently flooded. Its roots may lack oxygen despite being surrounded by water because air-filled soil spaces are lost and oxygen diffuses slowly through water. Drainage can improve aeration; it is not explained by saying roots need no water.
lessons.summary: Plants exchange gases with their surroundings without mammalian lungs or a blood system.

lessons.title: Investigating food, plant transport and pulse rate
objectives: Interpret nutrient tests with positive and negative controls.
Evaluate plant water-transport investigations and their limitations.
Calculate pulse rate and prepare a clear biological investigation report.
paragraphs: Practical biology connects a question to a measurable response, with controls that test alternative explanations. Food analysis asks whether a detectable nutrient is present in a prepared sample; a plant-transport investigation follows water movement or estimates water uptake; a pulse investigation counts arterial pressure waves over time. These questions use different methods, so one procedure cannot substitute for another. In every case, define the sample, record the method, collect results with units and separate the observed result from the broader conclusion.

Under teacher supervision, iodine solution can indicate starch by a blue-black colour. Benedict’s reagent can indicate reducing sugars after the prescribed water-bath heating, with colour changes that may progress from blue towards green, yellow, orange or brick-red depending on conditions. The biuret test gives a lilac or purple colour in the presence of protein. A teacher-led ethanol emulsion test can indicate lipids by a milky emulsion after the specified mixing with water; ethanol must be kept away from ignition. These chemical tests must not be attempted by tasting samples or reagents, and a negative reducing-sugar test does not establish that every kind of carbohydrate is absent.

For a food test, a positive control contains a known target nutrient and should show the expected response; a negative control, often water, should not. Keep sample volumes, reagent amounts and any heating time comparable. If the positive control fails, a negative unknown cannot be interpreted confidently because the method may have failed. Food colour or cloudiness can mask results, and several nutrients may be present in one food. Detecting protein is not a complete assessment of a food’s nutritional value or its safety.

A teacher-prepared cut stem placed in coloured water can reveal coloured xylem pathways, supporting the location of water transport. It does not directly show sugar movement in phloem. A potometer measures water uptake through a cut shoot and is commonly used as an estimate of transpiration, but uptake is not identical to vapour loss because some water remains in tissues or is used in other processes. The apparatus must be watertight and prepared as instructed to avoid air entering the water column. Keep leaf area, temperature, light and humidity similar when investigating one chosen environmental factor.

A pulse can be counted at the wrist using light pressure with fingers rather than the thumb, whose own pulse can confuse the count. Count for a stated interval and convert to beats per minute if needed. Compare a resting period with gentle ordinary activity only under the school’s inclusive guidance; supplied data are a suitable alternative for anyone unable to participate. Keep posture, counting interval and timing after activity comparable, allow recovery and never use a classroom result as a medical diagnosis. Counting over very short intervals magnifies the effect of a one-beat error.

A report states the question, prediction, method, results, calculations, conclusion and limitations. In a pulse report, give actual counts and counting durations before converted rates. In a plant report, distinguish water uptake from the inferred transpiration rate. In a food report, list controls as well as unknown samples. Repeats and independent samples support reliability, but averaging cannot repair a systematically faulty method. Present data that do not fit the prediction, explain possible causes and recommend a change that directly addresses the identified limitation.
examples: A learner counts 18 pulses in 15 seconds. The converted rate is 18 × (60/15) = 72 beats per minute. A one-beat counting error would change the result by 4 beats per minute, showing why interval choice matters.

An unknown sample stays blue with Benedict’s reagent, but the known glucose control also stays blue after the same treatment. The unknown cannot be confidently classed as lacking reducing sugar because the test procedure or reagent may have failed.

A potometer records 0.8 mL water uptake in 10 minutes, giving 0.08 mL per minute. Calling this the measured uptake rate is accurate. Calling it the exact transpiration rate ignores water retained in tissues and possible apparatus effects.
lessons.summary: Practical biology connects a question to a measurable response, with controls that test alternative explanations.

lessons.title: Reaction types in fuels, food and everyday materials
objectives: Classify combination, decomposition, displacement and combustion reactions.
Connect balanced equations with burning and digestion.
Distinguish reaction type from energy transfer and reaction rate.
paragraphs: Chemical reactions can be grouped by patterns in reactants and products. In combination, two or more reactants form one product; in decomposition, one reactant produces two or more products. In displacement, a more reactive element can replace a less reactive one from a suitable compound. These categories describe patterns rather than visible appearance. A reaction can fit more than one description: magnesium reacting with oxygen is both combination and combustion. Always show the equation or specify the criterion instead of treating the labels as mutually exclusive boxes.

Combustion is reaction with an oxidising agent, commonly oxygen, that transfers energy rapidly and often produces a flame. Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon in enough oxygen forms carbon dioxide and water. Limited oxygen may lead to incomplete combustion, producing carbon monoxide and/or carbon particles as well as other products. Carbon monoxide is colourless and poisonous, so fuel-burning equipment needs proper ventilation and safe operation. A yellow smoky flame can indicate incomplete combustion, but the absence of visible smoke does not prove that combustion gases are harmless.

Digestion connects reaction chemistry to living organisms. Enzymes accelerate the breakdown of large food molecules; many digestive reactions are hydrolysis, in which water participates in breaking bonds. Starch is broken down through smaller carbohydrates to glucose, proteins to smaller peptides and amino acids, and fats to fatty acids and glycerol in a school summary. Digestion is not the same as cellular respiration: digestion prepares absorbable nutrients, while respiration transfers energy from substances such as glucose inside cells. “Food breaks down” is too vague to identify which process is meant.

Reaction pattern, energy transfer and rate answer different questions. An exothermic reaction transfers energy to the surroundings; an endothermic process takes in energy from them. A fast reaction need not release more total energy than a slow one using the same amounts. A catalyst changes the rate of a reaction without being consumed overall, and enzymes are biological catalysts. To compare rates fairly, control quantities, temperature and exposed surface as appropriate. School combustion, displacement and heating investigations require teacher supervision; equations are models for interpreting reactions, not instructions for unsupervised mixing.
examples: For magnesium combustion, 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. There are two Mg atoms and two O atoms on each side. It is combination because the reactants form one product, and combustion because magnesium reacts energetically with oxygen.

For methane combustion, CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. Carbon balances at one atom, hydrogen at four and oxygen at four on each side. This equation represents complete combustion and does not describe every product when oxygen is limited.

For displacement in a suitable solution, Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Zinc replaces copper in the compound, while the sulfate group remains unchanged in this overall equation. The equation is balanced with coefficients of one throughout.
lessons.summary: Chemical reactions can be grouped by patterns in reactants and products.

lessons.title: Speech sounds, word stress and careful listening
objectives: Distinguish meaning-changing vowel and consonant contrasts.
Mark syllables and stress without confusing spelling with sound.
Use a partner and a dictionary pronunciation guide to improve clarity.
paragraphs: Pronunciation is the production of speech sounds so that a listener can recognise words. English spelling is an imperfect guide: one letter may represent several sounds and several letters may represent one sound. Listen to a model when one is available, repeat the whole word, and then use it in a sentence. This chapter gives text guides, not an audio recording. A teacher or partner can read the practice words aloud; do not claim to have heard a recording when you have only read its script.

A minimal pair consists of two words with one sound difference and different meanings. Ship /ʃɪp/ and sheep /ʃiːp/ contrast the vowels /ɪ/ and /iː/. The contrast involves vowel quality as well as usual duration: simply stretching every short vowel will not produce a correct long vowel. Say “The ship arrived” and “The sheep arrived”; context changes, but careful sound production also helps. Lip and leap offer another example of the same contrast.

Consonants can change meaning too. Thin begins with /θ/: let air pass between the tongue tip and upper front teeth without vibrating the voice. Tin begins with /t/, a brief complete blockage followed by release. This text description helps placement but does not replace listening to speech. For /ð/ in this, the voice vibrates. Accents vary, so use an intelligible model consistently and listen respectfully to classmates.

A syllable is a spoken beat. In the guides TA-ble and be-GIN, capital letters show the stronger syllable; they do not instruct you to shout. Stressed syllables are generally clearer and more prominent. TA-ble has first-syllable stress, while be-GIN has final-syllable stress. Write /ˈ/ immediately before the stressed syllable when using dictionary notation. Word stress can distinguish RE-cord, a noun, from re-CORD, a verb, in many English varieties.

Words can share a pronunciation while having different spellings and meanings. One and won are homophones in common English pronunciations. They are not minimal pairs because there is no sound difference between them. Read the whole sentence before choosing a spelling: “Our team won one match.” A dictionary may show both pronunciation and word class. Check the entry that fits the intended meaning rather than assuming a spelling always identifies a sound.

Use a feedback cycle: choose a contrast, listen to a model, speak, ask what the listener understood, and try again. A useful listener writes the word heard before seeing the speaker’s card. If a pair is confused, practise it inside a meaningful sentence before repeating the test. Keep a small record of the intended word, the word recognised, and the next step. Improvement means clearer communication; it does not require imitating another person’s identity.
examples: Vowel contrast in context — Explain the difference between “Please sit” and “Take a seat”. — Sit /sɪt/ contains /ɪ/; seat /siːt/ contains /iː/. The sentences have different grammar but both request a sitting position. Practise the contrasting words separately and then in their full sentences.

Stress and word class — Read “Keep a record” and “We record results”. — In a common pronunciation, the noun is RE-cord and the verb is re-CORD. Meaning and position in the sentence identify the word class. Marking the stronger syllable helps the listener recognise the intended word.

Choosing a homophone spelling — Complete: “Asha ___ the race by ___ metre.” — “Asha won the race by one metre.” Won is the past form of win; one is a number. The sounds alone do not distinguish these spellings, so sentence meaning supplies the answer.
lessons.summary: Pronunciation is the production of speech sounds so that a listener can recognise words.

lessons.title: Listening, paraphrasing and responding to messages
objectives: Take accurate notes from an original oral-message script.
Distinguish a requirement from a suggestion.
Paraphrase details and ask useful clarification questions.
paragraphs: Listening is active work: identify the speaker’s purpose, select useful facts, and check whether your understanding is accurate. Before a message begins, prepare spaces for who, what, where, when and action. On a first hearing, aim for the main point. On a second hearing, check names, quantities, changes and conditions. The original script below is written text for a teacher or partner to read aloud. It is not an audio file. Reading it independently practises comprehension but does not demonstrate listening ability.

Original announcement script: “Good morning, Form One. Our reading club will meet on Thursday at 3:30 in Room Four because the library is being cleaned. Bring a notebook and one book that you are willing to discuss; do not bring money. A book exchange is suggested for next month, but it has not been approved. If you cannot attend, tell Salma before lunch on Thursday. The meeting will finish at 4:15 so that members can catch the school bus. Thank you.”

The main message is the arrangement for Thursday’s reading-club meeting. Required actions are to bring a notebook and a book, and to notify Salma before lunch if absent. The room has changed because of cleaning; the announcement does not say the club has stopped using the library permanently. The exchange is a suggestion, not a confirmed event. Words such as suggested, must, may and has not been approved prevent a listener from turning a possibility into a promise.

Original follow-up dialogue script: “Juma: Did she say we should pay for the exchange? Rehema: No. She said not to bring money, and the exchange is only a proposal. Juma: I will be at the clinic on Thursday afternoon. Rehema: Then tell Salma before lunch. Juma: Can I send my book with you? Rehema: Ask Salma whether that is acceptable; the announcement did not explain it.” Notice how Rehema distinguishes stated information from a question that needs further checking.

A paraphrase preserves meaning in new words. “The club will use Room Four on Thursday while the library is cleaned” accurately restates the location and reason. “The library is closed for a month” invents information. A summary is shorter and selects major points; a paraphrase can be about the same length as its source. Neither should add an opinion disguised as a fact. Use quotation marks only when you reproduce someone’s exact words.

Responses should serve the purpose of the message. An acknowledgement confirms receipt; a clarification question identifies missing information; an action follows an instruction. “I cannot attend; I will notify Salma before lunch” is relevant. “Will the same room be used next week?” is a sensible question, but the answer is not available in this announcement. After listening, compare notes with a partner, return to the script to settle disagreements, and correct your own record.
examples: Separating definite and possible events — Is the book exchange definitely happening next month? — No. “Suggested” and “has not been approved” show that it is only proposed. An accurate note is “Exchange proposed; confirmation pending.”

Paraphrasing an instruction — Restate “If you cannot attend, tell Salma before lunch on Thursday.” — Anyone who will miss the meeting should inform Salma on Thursday before the lunch break. The person, deadline and condition remain unchanged.

An appropriate response — You are unable to attend. What should you say? — “Salma, I cannot attend Thursday’s reading-club meeting because I have an appointment. I am telling you before lunch as requested.” This reports the relevant action without claiming that sending a book is permitted.
lessons.summary: Listening is active work: identify the speaker’s purpose, select useful facts, and check whether your understanding is accurate.

lessons.title: Retelling events, explaining routines and giving directions
objectives: Retell an original story in a logical sequence.
Distinguish routines from actions happening now.
Give usable directions with landmarks and sequence words.
paragraphs: A retelling preserves the important events and their relationships while using the teller’s own words. Read the story, identify the difficulty, the response and the outcome, and then make a brief sequence plan. Do not memorise every sentence. A listener should understand who acted, why the action mattered and how one event led to the next. Words such as first, later, meanwhile and finally help when they reflect the actual order.

Original story, “The missing sign”: Every Saturday, Neema helps at the village reading room. One wet morning she found two visitors waiting outside the old store. They had followed a wooden sign that still pointed to the former reading room. Neema first greeted them and explained that the books had moved to the community hall. She walked with them past the water tank and stopped at the hall’s blue door. Inside, her friend Baraka was arranging chairs. Neema told him about the misleading sign. After the visitors had selected books, the two friends asked the caretaker for permission to move it. The caretaker agreed and checked the arrow before they fixed the sign beside the path. The following Saturday, new visitors reached the hall without asking for help.

The story uses the simple past for completed actions: found, greeted, walked and agreed. “Every Saturday, Neema helps” describes a routine in the simple present. “Baraka was arranging chairs” shows an action in progress at that past moment. When describing a scene now, use the present progressive: “Baraka is arranging chairs.” The choice of tense follows time and meaning rather than a rule that every verb in one paragraph must look identical.

Directions need a starting point, a destination and an ordered route. In the story, the route starts at the old store, goes past the water tank and ends at the blue door of the community hall. These landmarks are useful because a visitor can recognise them. Do not say “turn left” unless you know the person’s starting position and facing direction. A map and spoken instructions should agree; an unmarked shortcut can confuse a first-time visitor.

A routine timetable explains repeated actions with clear times. “On Saturdays, Neema opens the room at nine and sorts books at half past nine” is a possible new routine, not a fact stated in the story. Label invented extensions clearly. Possessives also help identify objects: “Neema’s notebook” belongs to Neema; “their books” refers to books associated with the visitors. An apostrophe marks possession in a singular person’s name but is not added to the possessive pronoun theirs.

Practise retelling to a partner who has not read the story. Speak clearly, use a manageable pace and pause between stages. Invite a question at the end: an unclear referent such as “he moved it” may need the names or object repeated. Then retell in fewer words while keeping the problem, response and outcome. Accuracy matters more than an elaborate performance that invents motives or events.
examples: A sequence plan — Reduce the story to four stages. — Visitors follow an outdated sign; Neema guides them to the hall; the friends obtain permission and correct the sign; later visitors find the hall successfully. This keeps the causal chain.

Routine and current action — Contrast a weekly habit with an activity occurring now. — “Neema helps every Saturday” is a habit in the simple present. “Neema is helping a visitor now” is an ongoing action in the present progressive.

Directions from a known starting point — Guide a visitor from the old store to the reading room. — “Start at the old store. Follow the path past the water tank. Continue to the community hall and enter through the blue door.” These directions use only landmarks supplied by the story.
lessons.summary: A retelling preserves the important events and their relationships while using the teller’s own words.

lessons.title: Reasoned group discussion and responsible online replies
objectives: Support and challenge proposals using evidence.
Manage turns with respectful verbal and non-verbal cues.
Write clear online replies without spreading unverified claims.
paragraphs: A group discussion aims to examine an issue and reach a clearer understanding or decision. A useful contribution states a position, supplies a reason and connects to what another person has said. Agreement alone does not prove a proposal is sound, and disagreement need not attack a person. Define the actual decision before debating it. “Which two afternoons should the club use the field?” is more manageable than “What is wrong with school sport?”

Original discussion script for a reader to perform; this is text, not audio: “Chair: We can use the field on two afternoons. Which days should we request? Amina: I suggest Tuesday and Thursday because our club has no lessons after three on those days. Paulo: Tuesday suits me, but the field is already booked for a match on Thursday. I checked the notice this morning. Amina: Thank you. Could we use Friday instead? Fatma: Friday gives us a second session, although some members attend the science club then. Chair: Let us check how many are affected before deciding. Paulo: I can ask them today and report tomorrow.”

The claim about Thursday is supported by Paulo’s stated check of the notice. The group should still confirm the booking with the responsible person before requesting a new arrangement. Fatma introduces a competing need rather than rejecting sport altogether. The final decision is postponed until participation information is collected. A faithful report must not say that Friday has already been chosen. Responsible speakers can acknowledge uncertainty while keeping work moving.

Use expressions that describe the relationship between ideas: “I agree with the aim because…”, “I see a difficulty with that date…”, and “Could we compare the two options?” Allow a speaker to finish before raising a hand or using the agreed signal. A relaxed posture and an attentive orientation can show interest, but eye contact and gestures have different meanings in different communities. Do not assume that a quiet participant lacks ideas; invite a contribution without pressure.

Online group replies need a clear reference because participants may read messages hours later. “About Thursday’s field booking: the notice says it is reserved for a match” is clearer than “That is wrong.” Before forwarding a claim, ask who issued it, when it was issued and whether the current source supports it. Avoid posting classmates’ phone numbers or personal explanations for absence without permission. A screenshot is not automatically reliable or current.

A chair can keep a decision log with proposal, evidence, unanswered question, action owner and deadline. At the end, summarise what was agreed and what remains open. An effective closing here is: “Paulo will ask science-club members today; we will review his report tomorrow. Tuesday is suitable, but the second day is not settled.” This helps absent members understand the discussion and prevents a tentative idea from becoming an invented decision.
examples: A respectful counterargument — Challenge the suggestion of Thursday using the script. — “Thursday may not be available because this morning’s notice lists a match. Could we confirm the booking and compare another day?” It identifies evidence, proposes checking and keeps the discussion open.

Accurate digital reply — Reply to “Friday training is confirmed!” — “Friday was suggested, but the group has not confirmed it. Paulo will check how many science-club members are affected and report tomorrow.” This corrects the claim without blaming the sender.

A decision-log entry — Record the unresolved issue. — Issue: second training day. Options: Thursday or Friday. Evidence: Thursday match booking; Friday science-club clash for some members. Action: Paulo asks affected members today. Review: tomorrow. No final second day yet.
lessons.summary: A group discussion aims to examine an issue and reach a clearer understanding or decision.

lessons.title: Requesting services, negotiating prices and describing locations
objectives: Make precise, courteous service requests.
Use quantifiers and location expressions accurately.
Negotiate a price without misrepresenting agreement.
paragraphs: A service request explains what is needed and provides the details the provider needs to act. “Could you print twelve copies of this two-page notice, please?” is more useful than “Help me.” Add a deadline, ask about cost and check whether the service is possible. Courteous expressions include could you, may I and I would like. Politeness is not a promise that the answer must be yes; listen to limits and agree on a realistic next step.

Original shop dialogue script, supplied as text for role-play: “Customer: Good afternoon. I would like twelve exercise books for our study group. Do you have enough of the eighty-page ones? Seller: Yes. They are two thousand shillings each. Customer: That is twenty-four thousand altogether. Could you offer a lower price for twelve? Seller: I can sell the twelve for twenty-two thousand. Customer: Thank you. Does that include a bag? Seller: Yes, one paper bag. Customer: We can pay twenty-one thousand. Would you accept that? Seller: I am sorry; twenty-two thousand is my lowest total. Customer: Then we will take six today at the usual price. Seller: Certainly; that is twelve thousand.”

The customer checks availability before negotiating. The quoted unit price is two thousand, so twelve books normally cost twenty-four thousand. A proposed reduction is not a completed sale: the seller does not accept twenty-one thousand. The actual final agreement is six books at the usual unit price, costing twelve thousand. When paraphrasing, preserve both quantity and price. A confident tone should never turn a rejected offer into an accepted contract.

Quantifiers tell listeners how much or how many. Use many and a few with countable plural nouns: many books, a few bags. Use much and a little with uncountable nouns: much paper, a little ink. Some and enough can fit both: some books, some paper, enough books, enough ink. “A few books” means a small positive number; “few books” suggests an insufficient or disappointingly small number in many contexts.

Location descriptions should establish a reference point. Imagine a service centre with a reception desk just inside the entrance, a photocopy counter to the left of reception and a payment desk opposite the counter. “The payment desk is opposite the photocopy counter” names both the place sought and its reference feature. Left and right depend on orientation; tell a visitor to face reception first. Use near, beside, behind and between only when the arrangement actually supports them.

A request conversation usually opens with a greeting, states the need, clarifies details, negotiates if appropriate, confirms the agreement and closes courteously. If a provider cannot help, ask for an alternative instead of repeating the same demand. “When would it be ready?” and “Could you recommend another service?” move the exchange forward. Confirm the amount, quantity and delivery time before paying. Keep an accurate written record when the request concerns a group.
examples: Confirming the actual deal — How much is paid in the final shop agreement? — Six books × 2,000 shillings = 12,000 shillings. The 22,000 offer applied to twelve books, and the 21,000 counteroffer was rejected. Neither is the final payment.

A precise printing request — Improve “I need some copies soon.” — “Could you print twelve copies of this two-page notice by 2 p.m., please? How much will they cost?” The quantity, document, deadline and price question are clear.

Directions with an orientation — Direct a visitor to the photocopy counter in the imagined centre. — “Enter the centre and face the reception desk. The photocopy counter is on your left. The payment desk is opposite it.” This fixes the viewpoint before using left.
lessons.summary: A service request explains what is needed and provides the details the provider needs to act.

lessons.title: Combining oral sources and presenting a coherent report
objectives: Separate facts, estimates and recommendations in two original scripts.
Synthesise shared and differing information.
Use cohesive devices and intonation to present a balanced report.
paragraphs: Synthesis combines relevant ideas from more than one source around a question. It is not two unrelated summaries placed side by side. Start with a purpose, such as “What should our club recommend about the school garden?” Take separate notes for each speaker before grouping them into themes. Record who said what, because two speakers may use different evidence or speak about different times. Do not manufacture agreement to make a report simpler.

Original oral-source script A, gardener: “We planted forty bean seedlings on Monday. By Friday, thirty-four were standing upright; six had wilted. The bed beside the wall stayed damp longer than the bed beside the path. I think the path bed needs mulch, but we have not tested that idea. Please keep the gate closed because goats entered last term. I can demonstrate mulching on Wednesday after class.” This is a text script for a human reader, not recorded audio.

Original oral-source script B, student observer: “Our group counted thirty-five upright seedlings on Thursday, before Friday’s hot afternoon. We noticed that two watering cans leak. We have not measured how much water they lose. We recommend repairing the cans before buying more. Wednesday after class clashes with our debate practice, but two members can attend the gardener’s demonstration and report back. We should compare the two beds for a week before deciding whether mulch helps.” This second source is also original text for reading aloud.

The counts of thirty-five and thirty-four are from different days, so they are not necessarily contradictory. It is possible for one additional plant to wilt between observations; the scripts do not establish the cause. Both speakers favour practical action, but their priorities differ: the gardener proposes mulch and a closed gate, while students mention leaking cans and a comparison. The wall bed’s dampness is observed; the claim that mulch will help is an untested explanation.

Organise a report by themes: seedling condition, water management, animal protection and participation. A report might say, “Thirty-four of forty seedlings were upright on Friday. The gardener observed more lasting moisture beside the wall, while students found two leaking cans. We therefore recommend repairing the cans and comparing the beds before judging the mulch proposal.” Therefore signals a conclusion, while introduces a comparison, and before marks an order. Use each connector for a real logical relationship.

When presenting orally, group words into meaningful phrases and pause between points. In many varieties of English, a completed statement often ends with a falling pitch, while a genuine yes/no question may end with a rising pitch. Patterns vary with intention and accent; do not impose one pattern mechanically. Emphasise important contrasts, such as Thursday versus Friday, without shouting. End by distinguishing agreed actions, proposals and unanswered questions, then invite clarification.
examples: Reconciling counts — Do 35 upright seedlings on Thursday and 34 on Friday prove one observer wrong? — No. The observations concern different days. One plant may have wilted later, but that explanation remains possible rather than proven. Report both dates accurately.

A thematic synthesis — Combine the water-related information in one statement. — “The wall bed remained damp longer, and students found two leaking cans; repairing the cans and comparing beds would give the group better evidence for water-management decisions.” This combines observations without calling the mulch proposal tested.

A logical connector — Connect “Wednesday clashes with debate practice” and “Two members can attend”. — “Although Wednesday clashes with debate practice, two members can attend the demonstration and report back.” Although correctly introduces a concession.
lessons.summary: Synthesis combines relevant ideas from more than one source around a question.

lessons.title: Usimulizi wa matukio: kiimbo, mkazo na mpangilio
objectives: Kusimulia tukio kwa mfuatano unaoeleweka.
Kutofautisha kiimbo, mkazo na lafudhi katika usemaji.
Kutumia sauti na mapumziko kuwasilisha maana kwa ufasaha.
paragraphs: Usimulizi ni utoaji wa habari kuhusu matukio kwa njia inayomwezesha msikilizaji kufuatilia wahusika, mahali, wakati na matokeo. Kabla ya kusimulia, panga mwanzo unaotambulisha hali, kiini chenye tukio kuu na mwisho unaoonesha kilichotokea. Usichanganye taarifa ulizoshuhudia na ulizosikia kwa wengine. Ukiongeza tukio la kubuni kwa mazoezi, litambulishe kuwa la kubuni. Mpangilio mzuri husaidia msikilizaji kuelewa sababu ya hatua fulani badala ya kukariri orodha ya vitendo.

Hadithi asilia, “Kikapu cha vitabu”: Siku ya Jumatano, Amina na Sudi walipeleka vitabu kwenye kona ya kusoma ya kijiji. Walipofika darajani, waliona maji yamefunika sehemu ya njia. Sudi alitaka kupita pembeni, lakini Amina alikumbuka onyo la kutokaribia mkondo wakati wa mvua. Walisimama mbali na maji na kumpigia mlezi wao simu. Mlezi aliwaelekeza watumie njia ya sokoni yenye daraja salama. Walifika wakiwa wamechelewa kwa dakika ishirini, lakini vitabu vilikuwa vikavu. Amina aliwaeleza wasomaji sababu ya kuchelewa. Baadaye, watoto walichora ramani ya njia salama na kuiweka ukutani. Siku iliyofuata, kikundi kingine kilitumia ramani hiyo kufika bila kukaribia maji.

Kiimbo ni kupanda na kushuka kwa sauti katika tungo. Kauli “Umefika.” na swali “Umefika?” zinaweza kuwa na maneno yale yale lakini zikawa na nia tofauti. Alama za uandishi hutoa mwongozo katika matini, ila sauti halisi hutegemea muktadha na kusudi la mzungumzaji. Katika usimulizi, sauti ya mshangao inaweza kuonesha hali ya ghafla; usitumie mshangao katika kila sentensi kwani tofauti za maana zitapotea.

Mkazo wa neno ni uzito unaowekwa kwenye silabi fulani. Katika maneno mengi ya Kiswahili sanifu, mkazo huwa kwenye silabi ya pili kutoka mwisho: ki-TA-bu, ki-KA-pu, a-me-FI-ka. Herufi kubwa hapa ni alama ya kufundishia, si sehemu ya tahajia ya kawaida. Mkazo wa tungo unaweza kulipa neno fulani uzito wa ujumbe: “AMINA alipiga simu” humtambulisha mtendaji, ilhali “Amina alipiga SIMU” husisitiza njia aliyotumia. Msisitizo huo hausababishi kubadili tahajia.

Lafudhi ni namna ya kutamka inayohusishwa na mazingira ya lugha ya msemaji. Tofauti za lafudhi hazimpi mtu thamani ndogo. Lengo la mazoezi ni kueleweka na kutumia matamshi yanayofaa kwa hadhira, si kudhihaki asili ya mtu. Matini hii hutoa maelekezo ya maandishi; haina faili ya sauti. Mwalimu au mwenzi anaweza kusoma mifano ili mwanafunzi asikilize, ajaribu na kupata mrejesho kuhusu uelewekaji.

Katika utendaji, simama au kaa kwa namna inayokuruhusu kupumua vizuri, tamka kwa kasi ya wastani na pumzika kwenye mipaka ya mawazo. Tumia “kwanza”, “baadaye” na “mwishowe” panapofaa, bila kuzirudia bila sababu. Unaporipoti sababu ya kuchelewa kwa wahusika, eleza kuwa walichagua njia salama; usibuni kuwa daraja lilivunjika. Mwombe msikilizaji ataje tatizo na suluhisho alilosikia, kisha rekebisha sehemu iliyoleta utata.
examples: Mpango wa masimulizi — Panga hadithi ya kikapu katika hatua nne. — Kwanza watoto wanapeleka vitabu. Kisha wanakuta njia imefunikwa na maji. Wanaomba ushauri na kutumia njia salama. Mwishowe wanafika na kuandaa ramani inayosaidia wengine. Mpango huu unabaki na tatizo, hatua na matokeo.

Mkazo wa neno — Weka mkazo wa kufundishia katika neno kikapu. — Gawa neno katika silabi: ki-ka-pu. Hesabu kutoka mwisho: pu ni ya kwanza, ka ni ya pili. Kwa hiyo weka ki-KA-pu. Herufi kubwa zinaonesha mkazo tu; tahajia ya kawaida ni kikapu.

Msisitizo wa ujumbe — Eleza tofauti ya “AMINA alipiga simu” na “Amina alipiga SIMU”. — Ya kwanza inasisitiza kwamba Amina ndiye mtendaji. Ya pili inasisitiza simu kama njia ya mawasiliano. Maneno yanaendelea kuandikwa kawaida katika matini isiyo na alama za mazoezi.
lessons.summary: Usimulizi ni utoaji wa habari kuhusu matukio kwa njia inayomwezesha msikilizaji kufuatilia wahusika, mahali, wakati na matokeo.

lessons.title: Kusikiliza mazungumzo na kuandika muhtasari mwaminifu
objectives: Kutambua maamuzi, mapendekezo na taarifa zisizokamilika.
Kuchukua dondoo kutoka hati asilia ya mazungumzo.
Kutoa muhtasari usioongeza madai mapya.
paragraphs: Kusikiliza kwa umakini kunahitaji kuelewa kusudi la mazungumzo, si kukumbuka kila neno. Jiandae kwa maswali: nani anasema, anazungumzia nini, lini na hatua ipi inahitajika? Sikiliza mara ya kwanza ili kupata ujumbe wa jumla na mara ya pili kuhakiki idadi, muda na masharti. Hati inayofuata ni maandishi asilia ya kusomwa kwa sauti na mwalimu au mwenzi; si faili ya sauti. Ukiisoma mwenyewe, umefanya ufahamu wa maandishi badala ya kuonesha uwezo wa kusikiliza.

Hati asilia ya mazungumzo: “Mwenyekiti: Tumekutana kupanga siku ya usafi wa kona ya kusoma. Neema: Jumamosi saa mbili asubuhi inafaa, lakini vitabu vihamishwe kwanza ili visilowane. Musa: Nitaleta boksi mbili. Hata hivyo, sijapata jibu la mwenye mkokoteni wa kubeba meza. Mwenyekiti: Basi tusitangaze kuwa mkokoteni upo. Asha: Tunaweza kusafisha rafu bila kuhamisha meza? Neema: Ndiyo, lakini sakafu yote itasubiri mpaka meza zihamishwe. Musa: Nitamuuliza tena mwenye mkokoteni leo jioni. Mwenyekiti: Tumekubaliana kuanza na rafu Jumamosi saa mbili asubuhi. Uamuzi wa kuosha sakafu utategemea taarifa ya mkokoteni.”

Katika hati hiyo, kuanza na rafu kumekubaliwa; kuosha sakafu kuna sharti ambalo halijatimizwa. Musa amesema ataleta boksi mbili na kuuliza kuhusu mkokoteni. Hajasema mwenye mkokoteni amekubali. Maneno “sijapata jibu” na “utategemea” yanaweka mipaka ya uhakika. Msikilizaji mwaminifu anayarekodi ili tangazo lisiahidi kifaa ambacho bado hakijathibitishwa.

Dondoo ni maandishi mafupi ya kukumbusha taarifa muhimu. Unaweza kutumia vichwa kama muda, vifaa, tahadhari, maamuzi na kazi zinazofuatiliwa. Andika “Jumamosi, saa mbili asubuhi; rafu kwanza; boksi 2—Musa; mkokoteni—jibu halijapatikana”. Hizi ni dondoo, si lazima ziwe aya kamili. Lakini muhtasari wa kuwasilisha kwa wengine unahitaji sentensi zinazoungana na kuonesha wazi uhusiano wa masharti.

Muhtasari hupunguza mazungumzo huku ukibakiza mawazo makuu. Ondoa salamu na marudio ikiwa havihitajiki kwa kusudi lako. Usiondoe sharti linalobadili maana: “Wataosha sakafu Jumamosi” si mwaminifu kwa hati. Muhtasari sahihi unaweza kusema kuwa wataanza kusafisha rafu na kwamba kuosha sakafu kutategemea kupatikana kwa mkokoteni. Tumia maneno yako, lakini usibadili mhusika wa jukumu au muda uliotajwa.

Unaposhiriki majadiliano, toa nafasi kwa wengine na uulize swali maalumu. “Musa, utatupatia lini jibu kuhusu mkokoteni?” ni bora kuliko “Vipi sasa?” kwa sababu linaonesha taarifa inayohitajika. Lugha ya mkato inaweza kutumika baina ya walio na muktadha mmoja, lakini rekodi ya mwisho ihitaji uwazi. Maliza kwa kuthibitisha maamuzi na kazi: ni nani atafanya nini na taarifa itapatikana lini?
examples: Dondoo lenye sharti — Rekodi hali ya mkokoteni kwa maneno machache. — “Mkokoteni: haujathibitishwa; Musa afuatilie leo jioni.” Dondoo hili linatofautisha kifaa kinachohitajika na kifaa kilichopatikana.

Muhtasari sahihi — Fupisha uamuzi wa kikao kwa sentensi mbili. — “Kikundi kitaanza kusafisha rafu Jumamosi saa mbili asubuhi, baada ya kulinda vitabu. Kuosha sakafu kutategemea taarifa ya mkokoteni, ambayo Musa atafuatilia leo jioni.” Muda na sharti vimehifadhiwa.

Swali la kufafanua — Je, mkokoteni utapatikana bila malipo? — Hati haisemi kuhusu malipo. Swali linalofaa ni “Je, mwenye mkokoteni atahitaji malipo, na kama ndiyo, kiasi gani?” Usijibu kuwa ni bure bila taarifa.
lessons.summary: Kusikiliza kwa umakini kunahitaji kuelewa kusudi la mazungumzo, si kukumbuka kila neno.

lessons.title: Mazungumzo ya nyumbani, shuleni na hospitalini
objectives: Kuteua msamiati na kiwango cha urasmi kulingana na muktadha.
Kutoa maombi, maelezo na hoja kwa adabu.
Kutumia tafsida bila kuficha taarifa muhimu.
paragraphs: Muktadha ni jumla ya mazingira yanayoathiri namna ya kuwasiliana: mahali, uhusiano wa washiriki, umri, kusudi na hali ya tukio. Kauli inayotosha kwa rafiki wa karibu inaweza kutofaa katika ombi rasmi. Hii haimaanishi kuwa kila mzee au kila kijana atapenda mtindo uleule. Sikiliza mwitikio wa unayezungumza naye na rekebisha maneno yako kwa heshima. Ufasaha ni kueleza jambo kwa uwazi na mtiririko unaofaa, si kutumia maneno magumu bila sababu.

Mazungumzo asilia ya nyumbani: “Mtoto: Shikamoo, bibi. Naomba nikusaidie kupanga vyombo. Bibi: Marahaba. Asante; weka vikombe hapa, lakini usibebe sufuria yenye maji moto. Mtoto: Nimeelewa. Nitaanza na vikombe vilivyopoa.” Salamu hiyo inafaa katika jamii nyingi zinazotumia Shikamoo; desturi zinaweza kutofautiana. Msaidizi amethibitisha alichoelewa na kutambua mpaka wa usalama badala ya kusema tu “sawa” bila hatua iliyo wazi.

Mazungumzo asilia shuleni: “Mwanafunzi: Samahani, mwalimu. Naomba muda wa ziada wa kuwasilisha kazi. Nilifika nyumbani nikakuta daftari langu limeloweshwa na maji. Mwalimu: Unaweza kuleta nakala mpya kesho kabla ya kipindi cha kwanza? Mwanafunzi: Ndiyo. Je, nikamilishe maswali yote au yale yaliyoharibika tu? Mwalimu: Yote, ili niwe na kazi kamili.” Ombi linatoa sababu inayoweza kufuatiliwa, linakubali sharti na linauliza ufafanuzi. Haliwahakikishii wengine kuwa kila ombi la kuongeza muda litakubaliwa.

Mazungumzo asilia hospitalini: “Mgonjwa: Habari, naomba kuelekezwa sehemu ya mapokezi. Mhudumu: Iko mbele, karibu na mlango wa kijani. Mgonjwa: Asante. Nimekuwa na maumivu ya tumbo tangu jana; nitamweleza nani? Mhudumu: Mweleze mhudumu wa mapokezi akuelekeze hatua inayofuata.” Lugha ya heshima haipaswi kuficha dalili muhimu. Matini hii ni mazoezi ya lugha; uamuzi wa huduma hutolewa na wahudumu wa afya kwa hali ya mgonjwa.

Tafsida ni uteuzi wa maneno ya upole badala ya maneno yanayoweza kukera au kuumiza. “Amefariki” mara nyingi hutumiwa kwa upole kuhusu kifo. Hata hivyo, upole usilete utata unaozuia msaada. Katika maelezo ya tatizo, taja kinachohitajika, kilichotokea na muda wake kwa namna inayofaa. Epuka matusi, ubaguzi na kudhani kwamba jinsia au umri wa mtu humpa tabia fulani moja kwa moja.

Malumbano ya hoja ni kuchunguza mitazamo kwa sababu na ushahidi. “Ninapendekeza rafu ya ziada kwa sababu vitabu ishirini vimewekwa sakafuni” ina hoja inayoweza kukaguliwa. “Mtu yeyote asiyekubaliana hajui kitu” ni shambulio, si ushahidi. Unapokataa, eleza sehemu unayokataa na sababu, kisha pendekeza njia mbadala. Malizia mazungumzo kwa kuthibitisha hatua inayofuata, kutoa shukrani au kufunga mjadala kwa adabu.
examples: Ombi lenye sababu — Boresha “Nipe muda mwingine!” katika muktadha wa shule. — “Samahani, mwalimu. Naomba kuwasilisha nakala mpya kesho kwa sababu daftari langu limeloweshwa. Je, muda huo utakufaa?” Ombi linataja hitaji, sababu na uwezekano wa kukubaliwa.

Ufafanuzi wa maelekezo — Mwanafunzi afanye nini baada ya kupewa muda wa kesho? — Aulize iwapo atawasilisha maswali yote au yaliyoharibika tu. Baada ya jibu, athibitishe: “Nitaleta kazi yote kesho kabla ya kipindi cha kwanza.” Hii inazuia tafsiri mbili.

Pingamizi la heshima — Pinga kununua rafu bila kuchunguza mahitaji. — “Nakubaliana kuwa vitabu vinahitaji sehemu nzuri. Hata hivyo, ningependa tuhesabu nafasi iliyopo kwanza ili tujue ukubwa wa rafu tunaohitaji.” Kauli inaheshimu lengo na kuhoji hatua kwa sababu.
lessons.summary: Muktadha ni jumla ya mazingira yanayoathiri namna ya kuwasiliana: mahali, uhusiano wa washiriki, umri, kusudi na hali ya tukio.

lessons.title: Kusikiliza kwa udadisi na kuandika kumbukumbu za hoja
objectives: Kutofautisha taarifa, pendekezo na uamuzi katika habari changamani.
Kuuliza maswali yanayojaza mapengo ya taarifa.
Kuandika kumbukumbu zenye maamuzi, majukumu na muda wa utekelezaji.
paragraphs: Kusikiliza kwa udadisi ni kufuatilia ujumbe huku ukichunguza chanzo, maana na mapengo yake. Si kukatiza kila sentensi wala kukubali kila dai kwa sababu limesemwa kwa kujiamini. Andaa jedwali la hoja, ushahidi uliotajwa, swali na hatua. Unaposikia idadi, rekodi kipimo na kipindi chake: ndoo kumi kwa siku si sawa na ndoo kumi kwa wiki. Kama taarifa haijatolewa, andika kuwa haijatajwa badala ya kubuni jibu.

Hati asilia ya habari ya kusomwa kwa sauti; hii ni matini, si rekodi ya sauti: “Mratibu: Katika wiki iliyopita, wanafunzi walikusanya chupa mia moja na ishirini kutoka eneo la shule. Sabini zilipatikana karibu na uwanja, thelathini karibu na kantini na ishirini nyuma ya madarasa. Mlezi: Idadi hizo zinaonesha mahali pa kuanzia, lakini hatujui kama chupa zote zilitupwa wiki hiyo. Mwanafunzi: Ninapendekeza vyombo vitatu vya kukusanyia chupa viwekwe karibu na uwanja. Mhasibu: Tuna pesa za kununua vyombo viwili tu kwa sasa. Mratibu: Basi kamati ichunguze bei na njia ya kupata chombo cha tatu. Tusifanye ununuzi leo.”

Mwendelezo wa hati asilia: “Mwanafunzi: Je, chupa zitauzwa ili kupata fedha? Mlezi: Bado hatujathibitisha mnunuzi wala bei. Kwanza tutauliza wakusanyaji wawili wenye huduma inayoruhusiwa. Mratibu: Rehema na Doto watauliza bei za vyombo na kuleta taarifa Ijumaa. Mimi nitawasiliana na wakusanyaji kabla ya kikao hicho. Tumeamua kuanza kuhesabu chupa kila siku kutoka Jumatatu ijayo ili tujue mabadiliko. Mhasibu: Nitaandaa daftari lenye tarehe, eneo na idadi. Mlezi: Chupa zilizovunjika zishughulikiwe na mtu mzima mwenye vifaa vinavyofaa; wanafunzi wasiziokote kwa mikono.”

Taarifa iliyopo ni kwamba chupa 120 zilikusanywa wiki iliyopita; haijathibitishwa kuwa zote zilitupwa katika wiki hiyo. Pendekezo la vyombo vitatu halijawa agizo la kununua, kwa sababu fedha zinatosha viwili na kamati imeagizwa kuchunguza. Dai kwamba chupa zitauzwa kwa faida fulani pia halina msingi katika hati. Udadisi unahitaji kuuliza kuhusu mnunuzi, bei, gharama na usalama bila kudhani majibu.

Kumbukumbu za kikao si nakala ya kila neno. Zihifadhi mada, taarifa muhimu, maamuzi, majukumu na muda. Kwa mfano: “Rehema na Doto wachunguze bei za vyombo; taarifa Ijumaa.” “Mratibu awasiliane na wakusanyaji kabla ya kikao cha Ijumaa.” “Kuhesabu chupa kila siku kuanze Jumatatu ijayo.” Usiongeze tarehe ya kalenda ambayo haikutajwa; unaweza kuiacha wazi ili mratibu aiweke baada ya kuithibitisha.

Wasilisha mawazo makuu kwa uwazi na uwekevu. Uwekevu hapa ni kutumia maneno yanayotosha bila marudio yanayoficha ujumbe. Kwanza eleza hali, kisha tofauti kati ya kilichoamuliwa na kinachochunguzwa, halafu majukumu. Unapopokea swali la idadi, rudi kwenye dondoo: 70 + 30 + 20 = 120. Kujumlisha kunahakiki ulinganifu wa takwimu, lakini hakuthibitishi peke yake kwamba ukusanyaji ulifanywa kwa usahihi.
examples: Kuhakiki jumla — Je, takwimu za maeneo matatu zinakubaliana na jumla iliyosemwa? — Ndiyo: 70 + 30 + 20 = 120. Huu ni ulinganifu wa hesabu katika taarifa. Hatuwezi kutoka hapo pekee kuthibitisha kuwa kila chupa ilihesabiwa mara moja.
Kumbukumbu ya jukumu — Andika jukumu la Rehema na Doto bila kurefusha. — “Rehema na Doto: kuchunguza bei za vyombo; kuwasilisha taarifa Ijumaa.” Kumbukumbu inahifadhi wahusika, kazi na muda.

Swali la udadisi — Pendekeza swali kabla ya kutegemea fedha za kuuza chupa. — “Je, kuna mkusanyaji aliyethibitisha kununua, kwa bei gani na kwa masharti gani?” Hili linachunguza uwezekano badala ya kudai mapato ambayo hayajathibitishwa.
lessons.summary: Kusikiliza kwa udadisi ni kufuatilia ujumbe huku ukichunguza chanzo, maana na mapengo yake.

lessons.title: Kusoma kwa kina: ushahidi, maoni na muhtasari wa matini ndefu
objectives: Kuchunguza hoja za matini ndefu kwa kuzingatia ushahidi na mipaka yake.
Kutofautisha wazo kuu na mfano wake.
Kuandika muhtasari na maoni yanayoungwa mkono na matini.
paragraphs: Usomaji wa kina ni kufuatilia mawazo, uhusiano wake na namna mwandishi anavyoyaunga mkono. Kwanza pitia kichwa na muundo ili kutambua suala kuu. Kisha soma kila aya ukijiuliza: inaongeza hoja gani, inatoa ushahidi upi, na inaacha swali gani? Kusoma kwa utunduizi kunahitaji kuhoji bila kutafuta kosa katika kila sentensi. Mwandishi anaweza kuwa na hoja yenye manufaa ambayo bado inahitaji data zaidi. Tenganisha maneno ya matini na maoni utakayotoa wewe.

Matini asilia, “Maktaba inayotembea”, sehemu ya kwanza: Kijiji cha Mwangaza hakikuwa na jengo la maktaba. Watu waliotaka kusoma walitegemea vitabu vichache shuleni, ambavyo havingeazimwa kwa wote. Baada ya mkutano wa wazazi, kikundi cha vijana kilipendekeza boksi la vitabu litembezwe kutoka kitongoji kimoja kwenda kingine. Walipata vitabu sitini vya hadithi, kilimo na afya vilivyotolewa kwa hiari. Hakuna aliyedai kuwa boksi hilo lingechukua nafasi ya maktaba kamili; walitaka kuanza na huduma iliyowezekana kwa rasilimali walizokuwa nazo. Wazee wawili walipendekeza kila eneo liwe na mlezi wa boksi na daftari la kuazima.

Matini asilia, sehemu ya pili: Mwezi wa kwanza, boksi lilipelekwa katika vitongoji vitatu, likikaa wiki moja kila eneo na wiki moja kituoni kwa ukaguzi. Daftari lilionesha mikopo arobaini na miwili ya vitabu, lakini baadhi ya watu waliazima zaidi ya kitabu kimoja. Hivyo, mikopo hiyo haikumaanisha wasomaji arobaini na wawili tofauti. Watoto walipenda hadithi zenye michoro. Baadhi ya wakulima waliomba vitabu vyenye maelezo mafupi na picha kubwa kwa kuwa walikuwa na muda mdogo wa kusoma jioni. Mlezi alikusanya maombi hayo badala ya kuhitimisha kuwa watu hawapendi kusoma vitabu virefu katika hali zote.

Matini asilia, sehemu ya tatu: Tatizo lilijitokeza mvua iliponyesha siku ya kuhamisha boksi. Vijana walichelewesha safari na vitabu vikafika siku moja baada ya ratiba. Msomaji mmoja alilalamika kuwa hakupewa taarifa. Kamati ilikubali kasoro hiyo, ikaweka utaratibu wa kutuma ujumbe kwa walezi wa vitongoji mapema kila ratiba ilipobadilika. Pia iliamua kutafuta kifuniko kisichopitisha maji. Hata hivyo, hakukuwa na ushahidi wa gharama ya kifuniko bora; vijana walipewa kazi ya kulinganisha bei tatu kabla ya ununuzi. Mabadiliko hayo yalilenga kutatua tatizo maalumu badala ya kuficha kuchelewa kulikotokea.

Matini asilia, sehemu ya nne: Mwishoni mwa miezi mitatu, baadhi ya wanakijiji walitaka kununua vitabu vipya vyote vya hadithi, kwa sababu watoto walionekana kuvitumia sana. Wengine walikumbusha kwamba matumizi ya vitabu vya kilimo hayakufuatiliwa kwa makini; huenda watu walisoma pamoja bila kuazima. Kamati haikuchagua upande mara moja. Iliamua kuongeza kisanduku cha maoni na kuandika pia vipindi vya usomaji wa pamoja. Kwa maoni yangu kama msimulizi, nguvu ya mradi haikuwa kutokosea kabisa, bali kukubali mapungufu na kubadili utaratibu kwa taarifa mpya. Hata hivyo, mafanikio ya kijiji kimoja hayathibitishi kwamba mpango huu utatosha kila mahali.

Muhtasari wa matini hii unapaswa kuunganisha haja ya huduma, mpango wa boksi, data ya matumizi, tatizo la usafiri na hatua za kuboresha. Idadi ya mikopo ni ushahidi wenye mpaka; haiwezi kutafsiriwa moja kwa moja kuwa idadi ya watu. Kauli ya msimulizi kuhusu nguvu ya mradi ni maoni yenye sababu. Unapotoa maoni yako, rejea tukio au takwimu halisi na ueleze mipaka. Hoja “wanakijiji wote walipenda hadithi pekee” haiungwi mkono: matini inaonesha makundi na mahitaji tofauti.
examples: Kutafsiri takwimu kwa makini — Je, mikopo 42 inathibitisha wasomaji 42 tofauti? — Hapana. Baadhi ya watu waliazima zaidi ya kitabu kimoja. Idadi ya mikopo hupima miamala ya kuazima, si lazima watu tofauti.

Kutambua jibu la tatizo — Kamati ilikabilianaje na kuchelewa na ukosefu wa taarifa? — Ilikubali kasoro, ikaweka utaratibu wa ujumbe wa mapema na ikapanga kutafuta kifuniko kisichopitisha maji. Kununua kifuniko kulihitaji kulinganisha bei kwanza.

Maoni yenye ushahidi — Toa maoni yanayoungwa mkono kuhusu uamuzi wa kutonunua hadithi pekee mara moja. — “Uamuzi ulikuwa wa tahadhari kwa sababu matumizi ya vitabu vya kilimo hayakuwa yamefuatiliwa kikamilifu. Kisanduku cha maoni na rekodi za usomaji wa pamoja vinaweza kutoa taarifa zaidi kabla ya kutumia fedha.” Haya ni maoni, si nukuu ya matini.
lessons.summary: Usomaji wa kina ni kufuatilia mawazo, uhusiano wake na namna mwandishi anavyoyaunga mkono.

lessons.title: Mitindo ya mazungumzo, ishara na sentensi zilizounganishwa
objectives: Kurekebisha mtindo wa mazungumzo kulingana na uhusiano na kusudi.
Kutumia ishara zinazosaidia ujumbe bila kudhani maana yake kwa kila mtu.
Kutofautisha na kutumia sentensi ambatani na changamani katika mazungumzo.
paragraphs: Mtindo wa mazungumzo hutokana na uteuzi wa maneno, urefu wa kauli, kiwango cha urasmi na namna ya kubadilishana zamu. Mazungumzo ya marafiki yanaweza kuwa na kauli fupi kwa sababu wana taarifa za pamoja. Katika huduma rasmi, maelezo kamili husaidia mtu asiyejua hali yako. Umri, uhusiano na mazingira yanaweza kuathiri uteuzi, lakini usidhanie kwamba jinsia au umri humlazimisha kila mtu kupenda mtindo mmoja. Uliza na sikiliza kwa heshima.

Hati asilia ya mazungumzo ya marafiki: “Tunu: Umeona mpira? Kito: Upo kwa mlezi. Tuombe kabla ya mazoezi. Tunu: Sawa; nitamuuliza kama tunaweza kuutumia hadi saa kumi na moja. Kito: Ukiruhusiwa, niambie, nami nitawaita wenzetu.” Hati asilia ya ombi kwa mlezi: “Tunu: Shikamoo, mlezi. Naomba tuutumie mpira kwa mazoezi hadi saa kumi na moja, ikiwa uwanja uko wazi. Mlezi: Marahaba. Mnaweza kuutumia, lakini uwanja unahitajika saa kumi na nusu. Tunu: Asante; basi tutamaliza na kurudisha mpira kabla ya saa kumi na nusu.” Hizi ni hati za maandishi kwa maigizo, si sauti iliyorekodiwa.

Tunu anabadilisha mtindo bila kubadili ukweli wa hitaji lake. Kwa rafiki ametumia “Sawa” na rejea fupi; kwa mlezi ametaja ombi, mwisho wa muda na sharti la uwanja. Jibu la mlezi linaweka mpaka mpya wa saa kumi na nusu. Kurudia mpango uliorekebishwa kunaonesha uelewano. Kama Tunu angewaambia wenzake kuwa wamepewa hadi saa kumi na moja, angekuwa amepuuza sharti lililotolewa.

Ishara zinaweza kusaidia ujumbe: kuinua mkono kuomba zamu, kuonesha sehemu kwenye mchoro au kutikisa kichwa kuonesha kuwa unasikiliza. Hata hivyo, maana hutegemea jamii na muktadha. Kutikisa kichwa hakuthibitishi kila mara makubaliano; huenda ni ishara ya kufuatilia. Ikiwa uamuzi ni muhimu, thibitisha kwa maneno. Heshimu nafasi ya mtu na hitaji lake la kutotazamwa moja kwa moja; usilazimishe ishara moja kama kipimo pekee cha heshima.

Sentensi ambatani huunganisha vishazi huru viwili au zaidi: “Tunu atauliza ruhusa, na Kito atawaita wenzake.” Kila kishazi kinaweza kusimama kama taarifa kamili. Sentensi changamani ina kishazi kikuu na kishazi tegemezi: “Mkipata ruhusa, anzeni mazoezi.” Sehemu “mkipata ruhusa” hutoa sharti na haiwasilishi ujumbe kamili wa kujitegemea katika matumizi hayo. Viunganishi na viambishi vya masharti viwe na uhusiano wa maana, si mapambo ya kuifanya sentensi ionekane ndefu.

Fanya mazoezi ya kuanzisha, kuingilia kwa ruhusa, kubadili mada na kufunga mazungumzo. “Samahani kwa kuingilia; naomba kuthibitisha muda” husaidia kurekebisha jambo muhimu. “Kabla hatujamaliza, tuweke wazi nani atarudisha mpira” huleta hatua ya mwisho. Tumia sauti na ishara zinazolingana na maneno, halafu hakiki maana kwa kurudia makubaliano. Mazungumzo yenye mafanikio huwaacha washiriki wakijua kilichoombwa, kilichokubaliwa na kinachohitajika kufanywa.
examples: Kubadili kiwango cha urasmi — Badili “Tupatie mpira hadi jioni” kuwa ombi la mlezi lenye maelezo. — “Shikamoo, mlezi. Naomba tuutumie mpira kwa mazoezi hadi saa kumi na moja, ikiwa uwanja uko wazi.” Kauli ina salamu inayofaa katika muktadha, hitaji, kusudi, muda na sharti.

Sentensi ambatani — Unganisha “Tunu ataomba ruhusa” na “Kito atawaita wenzake”. — “Tunu ataomba ruhusa, na Kito atawaita wenzake.” Vishazi vyote viwili ni huru; kiunganishi na kinaunganisha vitendo viwili.

Kuthibitisha ishara — Mwenzi ametikisa kichwa baada ya kusikia muda wa kurudisha mpira. Uhakikisheje? — Uliza: “Tunakubaliana kurudisha mpira kabla ya saa kumi na nusu, sivyo?” Maneno yanathibitisha makubaliano badala ya kuitegemea ishara pekee.
lessons.summary: Mtindo wa mazungumzo hutokana na uteuzi wa maneno, urefu wa kauli, kiwango cha urasmi na namna ya kubadilishana zamu.

lessons.title: Asili, uhamaji na njia mbalimbali za kujikimu
objectives: Kutofautisha familia za lugha na utambulisho wa watu.
Kutumia ushahidi wa aina tofauti kueleza uhamaji na shughuli za jamii.
Kutathmini maadili bila kudhani jamii zote zilifanana.
paragraphs: Historia ya watu wa Tanzania inaelezwa kwa kuunganisha akiolojia, lugha, masimulizi na maandiko. Mabaki ya vyombo, mbegu na makazi huonyesha shughuli katika mahali na wakati fulani; hayaandiki moja kwa moja jina la kabila la watumiaji wake. Kufanana kwa maneno kunaweza kusaidia kuchunguza uhusiano wa lugha, lakini si uthibitisho kwamba wazungumzaji wote wana asili moja ya kibaolojia. Masimulizi ya ukoo yanaeleza jinsi watu wanavyokumbuka chimbuko lao; huchunguzwa pamoja na vyanzo vingine kwa sababu kumbukumbu zinaweza kuchagua au kuacha matukio.

Makundi yanayotajwa katika mtaala kama Wabantu, Wanilo, Wakushito na Wakichembe hayapaswi kugeuzwa kuwa visanduku vinavyowafunga watu. Kibantu ni kundi kubwa la lugha; lugha za Kinilo na Kikushito pia zina historia na matawi mbalimbali. Istilahi Wakichembe hutumika katika baadhi ya maelezo ya shule kwa jamii zinazohusishwa na lugha za mibofyo. Lugha za Kisandawe na Kihadza hazipaswi kudhaniwa kuwa lugha moja au ushahidi wa ukoo mmoja. Utambulisho hubadilika kwa ndoa, uhamaji, ujirani, biashara na maamuzi ya watu; kila madai ya asili yanahitaji ushahidi wake.

Uhamaji haukuwa safari moja yenye tarehe moja kwa watu wote. Watu walihama kwa kutafuta maji, malisho, ardhi, biashara au usalama, na wengine walibaki huku wakipokea wageni. Uhamaji unaweza kusambaza mbegu, ujuzi wa kufua chuma na maneno, lakini jambo linaloonekana baadaye katika eneo halithibitishi peke yake nani aliyelileta. Ili kupendekeza maelezo, mtafiti hulinganisha muda wa mabaki, mazingira, simulizi na ushahidi wa lugha. Kukubali kwamba jambo fulani bado halijulikani ni sehemu ya uaminifu wa kihistoria.

Kilimo, ufugaji, uvuvi, uwindaji, ukusanyaji, ufundi na biashara vilichanganyika kwa namna tofauti. Familia moja ingeweza kulima na kufuga huku ikibadilishana bidhaa na wavuvi au wafinyanzi. Katika mazingira yenye mvua isiyotabirika, kuchanganya shughuli kulisaidia kupunguza hatari ya njaa. Ziwa, bahari, udongo, wadudu na misimu viliweka fursa na vikwazo, lakini watu walifanya uchaguzi na kubuni mbinu. Hivyo si sahihi kusema kila mzungumzaji wa lugha fulani alikuwa mfugaji tu au mkulima tu; lazima tutaje eneo, kipindi na ushahidi.

Ushirikiano wa kazi, kuwasaidia wenye shida na kuhifadhi maarifa vilisaidia jamii kuendelea. Hata hivyo, kanuni zilikuwa tofauti na wakati mwingine mamlaka, umri au jinsia vilisababisha usawa mdogo wa kushiriki maamuzi. Kusoma historia kwa maadili hakumaanishi kusifu kila desturi. Tunachunguza nani alinufaika, nani alibebeshwa kazi, na njia zilizotumika kutatua migogoro. Darasani tunaweza kuthamini ukarimu na uaminifu huku tukikataa ubaguzi na kulinda haki na utu wa kila mtu.
examples: Mfano wa kuchambua dai: Mwanafunzi anasema chungu cha kale kinathibitisha kabila la mfinyanzi. Hatua ya kwanza ni kutambua ushahidi: chungu kinaonyesha ufundi na matumizi. Hatua ya pili ni kuangalia tarehe na eneo la ugunduzi. Hitimisho sahihi ni kwamba utambulisho wa watumiaji bado unahitaji ushahidi mwingine; umbo la chungu pekee halitoshi.

Mfano wa mazingira: Katika simulizi la kubuni kwa mazoezi, familia inavua ziwani na kulima karibu na kijito. Maji hutoa samaki na kumwagilia; mvua ikipungua, biashara ya samaki inaweza kusaidia kununua nafaka. Hii inaonyesha shughuli zinazosaidiana, si uthibitisho kwamba watu wote wa eneo hilo walifanya kazi hizo.

Mfano wa kulinganisha vyanzo: Simulizi linasema watu walihamia kwa ukame, na uchunguzi wa mazingira unaonyesha kipindi cha ukavu kinachokaribiana. Ushahidi huo unaunga mkono uwezekano wa ukame kuchochea uhamaji. Bado tunatafuta tarehe na sababu nyingine kama biashara; hatusemi ukame ndio sababu pekee.
lessons.summary: Historia ya watu wa Tanzania inaelezwa kwa kuunganisha akiolojia, lugha, masimulizi na maandiko.

lessons.title: Ukoo, mamlaka na uzalishaji kabla ya ukoloni
objectives: Kulinganisha mamlaka yaliyogawanyika na yaliyokusanyika.
Kueleza uhusiano wa uzalishaji, mgawanyo wa kazi na maadili.
Kutathmini manufaa na mipaka ya mifumo ya zamani.
paragraphs: Jamii za maeneo ya Tanzania kabla ya ukoloni hazikuwa na mfumo mmoja wa kuishi na kutawala. Katika sehemu fulani koo, familia, mabaraza na makundi ya rika yalikuwa na nafasi katika kufanya maamuzi. Katika nyingine kulikuwa na watawala waliokuwa na mamlaka juu ya eneo kubwa, wakisaidiwa na viongozi wa maeneo madogo. Maelezo ya mfumo lazima yataje eneo na kipindi kwa sababu taasisi zilibadilika. Kutokuwa na mfalme mmoja hakumaanishi kutokuwa na sheria, uongozi au utaratibu wa kutatua migogoro.

Ukoo uliweza kupanga wajibu wa kusaidiana, mahusiano ya kifamilia na matumizi ya ardhi. Baraza la wazee lingeweza kusikiliza mgogoro na kutafuta suluhu, lakini kiwango cha ushiriki wa vijana, wanawake na wageni kilitofautiana. Makundi ya rika yaliweza kushirikisha watu katika mafunzo, kazi au ulinzi. Taasisi hizo zilifundisha wajibu na heshima, ingawa heshima haipaswi kuchanganywa na kunyima mtu haki ya kusikilizwa. Uchunguzi wa maadili unahitaji kuangalia mchakato wa uamuzi na athari kwa kila upande.

Katika baadhi ya maeneo ya Unyamwezi na Uhehe, kwa nyakati tofauti, utawala ulihusisha viongozi wenye mamlaka yaliyokusanyika zaidi. Mamlaka hayo yangeweza kuratibu ulinzi, njia za biashara, ukusanyaji wa sehemu ya mazao na utekelezaji wa maamuzi. Hata ndani ya maeneo hayo hali haikuwa sawa wakati wote. Uwezo wa kukusanya rasilimali ungeweza kusaidia shughuli za pamoja, lakini pia ungeweza kutumika kulazimisha watu. Mchango wa mfumo haupimwi kwa ukubwa wa mamlaka tu, bali pia kwa usalama na ustawi wa watu.

Uchumi ulihusisha uzalishaji kwa matumizi ya familia pamoja na ubadilishanaji. Wakulima, wafugaji, wafua chuma, wafinyanzi na wafanyabiashara walihitaji bidhaa za wenzao. Kazi ziligawanywa kwa ujuzi, umri, jinsia au hali ya familia, lakini mgawanyo huo ulikuwa na tofauti na mabadiliko. Ardhi katika sehemu nyingi ilihusishwa na haki za matumizi kupitia jamii au familia; si sahihi kudhani kwamba kila mahali ilimilikiwa kwa utaratibu mmoja. Haki za kuvuna, kuchunga au kutumia maji zingeleta ushirikiano na pia migogoro.

Kazi ya pamoja katika shamba au ujenzi ingeweza kuimarisha mshikamano na kuongeza uzalishaji. Mamlaka yaliyolinda njia na masoko yangewezesha biashara, huku migogoro na vita vikipunguza usalama wa uzalishaji. Ili kutathmini mfumo, linganisha faida kama kusaidiana na mapungufu kama utegemezi, utumwa au kutoshiriki kwa baadhi ya watu. Uwepo wa maadili mazuri katika eneo moja hauondoi uwepo wa ukosefu wa haki katika eneo jingine. Tathmini bora hutumia mfano maalumu na kukubali tofauti za ndani.
examples: Kesi ya baraza: Familia mbili zinagombea eneo la kuchungia katika mfano wa kubuni. Suluhu yenye maadili huanza kwa kusikiliza pande zote, kutafuta ushahidi wa matumizi na kupanga maji na malisho bila kuzuia upande dhaifu. Baraza linalosikiliza familia moja pekee haliwezi kuitwa la haki kwa sababu tu ni la wazee.

Mfano wa uhusiano wa uchumi na mamlaka: Kiongozi akiweka ulinzi wa njia, mfua chuma anaweza kupeleka majembe sokoni kwa usalama. Wakulima wakipata majembe, uzalishaji unaweza kuongezeka. Hata hivyo, kodi kubwa kupita uwezo inaweza kupunguza faida; lazima tutathmini matumizi na mzigo wa ukusanyaji.

Mfano wa kulinganisha: Mfumo A una baraza la koo kadhaa; mfumo B una mtawala na viongozi wa maeneo. A unaweza kusambaza majadiliano lakini kuchelewa kuamua; B unaweza kuratibu haraka lakini kujilimbikizia mamlaka. Haya ni uwezekano wa kuchunguza, si sheria zinazothibitisha kila jamii.
lessons.summary: Jamii za maeneo ya Tanzania kabla ya ukoloni hazikuwa na mfumo mmoja wa kuishi na kutawala.

lessons.title: Biashara za mbali na mabadiliko ya teknolojia
objectives: Kueleza uhusiano wa pwani, bara na maeneo ya ngambo.
Kutumia mabaki kutathmini biashara bila kuyazidishia maana.
Kueleza vichocheo, manufaa na gharama za teknolojia.
paragraphs: Pwani ya Afrika Mashariki ilikuwa sehemu ya mitandao ya Bahari ya Hindi iliyounganisha bandari na maeneo ya Arabia, Uajemi, India na sehemu za Asia ya mbali. Upepo wa monsuni uliwezesha safari za meli katika misimu tofauti. Miji kama Kilwa ilikua kwa nyakati tofauti kabla ya ukoloni wa Ulaya wa karne ya kumi na tisa. Wakazi wa pwani walikuwa watendaji katika biashara na utamaduni wao, si wapokeaji wa mambo kutoka nje tu. Uhusiano huo ulihusisha biashara, makazi, ndoa, dini na mabadiliko ya lugha.

Bidhaa kutoka bara zilifika pwani kupitia mitandao iliyobadilika kwa karne nyingi. Pembe za ndovu na bidhaa nyingine ziliuzwa, huku nguo, shanga na baadhi ya vyombo vikiingia kutoka ngambo. Watu pia walitekwa na kuuzwa utumwani; kutaja biashara hiyo bila kueleza kulazimishwa na mateso kunapunguza ukweli wa historia. Katika karne ya kumi na tisa, misafara iliunganisha sehemu nyingi zaidi za bara na pwani. Si kila bidhaa ya kale iliyopatikana eneo moja ililetwa moja kwa moja na mfanyabiashara wa nchi ilikotengenezwa; bidhaa ingeweza kupita mikononi mwa wafanyabiashara kadhaa.

Ushahidi wa sarafu, vyombo na majengo husaidia kueleza biashara na mabadiliko ya miji. Kipande cha kauri kilichotengenezwa China kikikutwa Kilwa kinaonyesha bidhaa hiyo ilifika huko, lakini si uthibitisho wa idadi kubwa ya wahamiaji kutoka China. Maandishi, akiolojia na muda wa tabaka la ugunduzi vinapaswa kulinganishwa. Wareno waliingia katika biashara na siasa za pwani kuanzia mwisho wa karne ya kumi na tano, wakitumia nguvu katika maeneo kadhaa; baadaye ushawishi wa Oman uliongezeka. Mabadiliko haya hayakuwa na wakati au athari moja kwa pwani yote.

Sayansi na teknolojia za kabla ya ukoloni zilijumuisha kufua chuma, ufinyanzi, ujenzi, kutengeneza vyombo vya usafiri na kutumia maarifa ya mazingira. Uzalishaji wa chuma ulihitaji maarifa ya madini, joto, nishati na ufundi; chombo kilichokamilika hakikuonyesha hatua zote za kazi. Ufinyanzi ulitegemea kuchagua udongo, kuunda, kukausha na kuchoma kwa uangalifu. Maarifa haya yalifundishwa kwa mazoezi, uchunguzi na kushirikiana. Hayakuwa tuli: watu walibadilisha mbinu kutokana na mahitaji na rasilimali.

Biashara iliongeza mahitaji ya zana na ilileta ujuzi na vifaa vipya. Kuongezeka kwa watu, mahitaji ya chakula, mazingira na ushindani wa kisiasa pia vilichochea mabadiliko. Teknolojia inaweza kuongeza uwezo wa kulima au kusafiri, lakini matumizi mengi ya kuni yanaweza kupunguza miti na uzalishaji unaweza kutegemea kazi yenye unyonyaji. Tathmini nzuri hulinganisha faida, gharama na mgawanyo wa manufaa. Kusema teknolojia fulani ilikuwa bora kunahitaji kutaja kazi iliyofanywa, rasilimali zilizotumika na watu walioathirika.
examples: Mfano wa kauri: Kauri ya ngambo kwenye tabaka la kale la bandari huunga mkono mawasiliano ya kibiashara. Tunaanza kwa tarehe na mahali ilipopatikana, kisha kulinganisha na sarafu au maandiko. Hitimisho ni uhusiano wa bidhaa; uraia wa kila mkazi au safari ya moja kwa moja bado havijathibitishwa.

Mfano wa mnyororo wa zana: Madini na nishati hutumika kuyeyusha na kufua chuma; fundi hutengeneza jembe; mkulima hulitumia. Jembe linaweza kupunguza ugumu wa kazi, lakini upatikanaji wa ardhi, mvua na kazi huathiri mavuno pia. Zana moja si sababu pekee ya mabadiliko ya uchumi.

Mfano wa kuchagua teknolojia: Mafundi wa mfano wanataka kuongeza uchomaji wa vyungu. Huamua kukausha vyungu vizuri, kuboresha upangaji wa tanuru na kupanda miti kwa matumizi ya baadaye. Suluhu hiyo hutathminiwa kwa vyungu visivyovunjika, kiasi cha kuni na hali za kazi, si idadi ya vyungu pekee.
lessons.summary: Pwani ya Afrika Mashariki ilikuwa sehemu ya mitandao ya Bahari ya Hindi iliyounganisha bandari na maeneo ya Arabia, Uajemi, India na sehemu za Asia ya mbali.

lessons.title: Kutumia urithi kwa haki na kujenga uchumi wa ushirikiano
objectives: Kutofautisha urithi unaoshikika na usioshikika.
Kupanga matumizi ya urithi yanayolinda haki na mazingira.
Kuonyesha jinsi ushirikiano unavyoongeza thamani na uwajibikaji.
paragraphs: Urithi ni mambo yenye maana ambayo jamii hupokea, hutunza na kurithisha. Unaweza kuwa majengo, vitu na maeneo, au maarifa, lugha, muziki, hadithi na mbinu za kazi. Maana ya kitu hutegemea pia watu wanaokihusisha na maisha yao; si bei ya kuuza pekee. Urithi si jambo lililoganda: jamii huchagua jinsi ya kufundisha na kuutumia katika mazingira mapya. Kila matumizi yanahitaji kuuliza nani anautambua, nani anaruhusiwa kuueleza, na nani anapata manufaa.

Fursa za kiuchumi zinaweza kutoka katika ufundi, uongozi wa wageni, maonesho, vyakula na huduma za elimu. Fursa hizo zinahitaji ujuzi wa biashara kama kupanga gharama, kuweka kumbukumbu, kutangaza kwa uaminifu na kuwahudumia watu. Kuiga kazi ya mwingine na kuiuza bila makubaliano kunaweza kuvunja uaminifu na haki. Baadhi ya maarifa au maeneo yana masharti ya kijamii na kisheria; si kila jambo linalovutia wageni linapaswa kufanywa bidhaa. Ridhaa, heshima na maelezo sahihi ni sehemu ya thamani ya kazi.

Utunzaji huanza kwa kuandika taarifa sahihi, kuhifadhi mazingira na kuzuia uharibifu. Mwanafunzi hapaswi kuondoa kitu katika eneo la kihistoria, kuchimba bila ruhusa au kugusa mchoro ili kupata picha nzuri. Kuhifadhi maarifa kunaweza kuhusisha kurekodi simulizi kwa ridhaa na kuweka nakala salama. Hata picha au rekodi inaweza kuhitaji mipaka ya kutumiwa. Kutoa jina la mwenye maarifa na kuruhusu jamii kushiriki maamuzi husaidia kulinda urithi na utu wa watu.

Ushirikiano huunganisha uwezo wa watu katika uzalishaji, usafirishaji, masoko na huduma. Wafundi wanaweza kununua malighafi kwa pamoja, wakulima kushirikiana kuhifadhi mazao na wafanyabiashara kuunganisha uzalishaji na wanunuzi. Hii inaweza kupunguza gharama na kuongeza mapato, lakini haihakikishi faida bila usimamizi. Makubaliano ya majukumu, kumbukumbu za fedha, ukaguzi na utatuzi wa migogoro ni muhimu. Kikundi chenye watu wengi bila uwazi kinaweza kuwa na matatizo kuliko watu wachache wanaotekeleza wajibu wao.

Kukua kwa uchumi wa Taifa hutegemea watu kupata bidhaa na huduma, kuongeza ujuzi na kutumia rasilimali kwa tija. Ushirikiano kati ya maeneo unaweza kujenga kuaminiana kwa sababu washiriki hutegemeana na kutambua mchango wa wengine. Hata hivyo, ukuaji wa mapato pekee hauonyeshi ustawi wa kila mtu. Tathmini pia upatikanaji wa kazi yenye heshima, mgawanyo wa manufaa, ulinzi wa mazingira na nafasi ya watu wenye mahitaji tofauti. Maadili ya uaminifu na uwajibikaji hufanya ushirikiano uwe wa kudumu.
examples: Mfano wa hesabu ya ufundi: Kikundi cha mfano kinauza vikapu 10 kwa shilingi 8,000 kila kimoja; mapato ni 80,000. Gharama zote ni 55,000, hivyo ziada kabla ya mgawanyo ni 25,000. Kikundi kikitenga 10,000 kwa vifaa, 15,000 hubaki kwa mgawanyo kwa makubaliano. Mapato yote si faida.

Mfano wa uongozi wa wageni: Wanafunzi wanapanga ziara kwenye eneo la urithi. Wanaomba utaratibu kwa msimamizi, hutumia taarifa zilizokaguliwa, hufuata njia zinazoruhusiwa na hawachukui mabaki. Hivyo elimu na fursa za huduma vinaenda pamoja na utunzaji wa eneo.

Mfano wa haki ya simulizi: Msimulizi anakubali rekodi kwa darasa lakini hataki ichapishwe mtandaoni. Ridhaa hiyo ina mipaka. Suluhu ni kuitumia darasani tu, kuandika chanzo kwa makubaliano na kuomba ruhusa mpya kabla ya matumizi mapya; kupata rekodi si kupata haki zote.
lessons.summary: Urithi ni mambo yenye maana ambayo jamii hupokea, hutunza na kurithisha.

lessons.title: Mifumo ya kikoloni: utawala, uchumi na uhusiano wa nje
objectives: Kufuatilia mabadiliko ya utawala wa Tanganyika na Zanzibar.
Kulinganisha mifumo ya kiuchumi, kisiasa na kiutamaduni ya ukoloni.
Kutofautisha urithi wa miundombinu na haki ya kujitawala.
paragraphs: Ukoloni ni utawala wa nguvu ya kigeni juu ya eneo na watu wake, ukiwapa watawala wa nje uwezo wa kuamua mambo muhimu. Katika karne ya kumi na tisa, mataifa ya Ulaya yalipanua ushindani wa masoko, malighafi, maeneo ya uwekezaji na ushawishi wa kisiasa. Madai ya kuleta ustaarabu yalitumika kuhalalisha kutawala, lakini hayafuti matumizi ya nguvu na kunyimwa haki ya kujitawala. Mkutano wa Berlin wa 1884–1885 uliweka kanuni fulani za ushindani wa kikoloni barani Afrika; haukuwa tukio moja lililochora kila mpaka wa Tanzania ya leo.
