Tanganyika ya baadaye ilikuwa sehemu ya Afrika Mashariki ya Kijerumani kutoka mwisho wa karne ya kumi na tisa hadi Vita Kuu ya Kwanza ya Dunia. Utawala wa Wajerumani uliweka mamlaka, kodi na matumizi ya kazi katika uchumi uliolenga maslahi ya kikoloni. Mashamba ya bidhaa za kuuza, usafiri na taasisi za utawala zilikuzwa kwa maeneo na nyakati tofauti. Upanuzi huo ulihusisha unyakuzi wa mamlaka na mapambano ya wenyeji; haukuwa makubaliano huru ya wakazi wote. Uwepo wa reli au jengo haupaswi kuficha swali la nani alilipa gharama na nani aliweka vipaumbele.

Baada ya vita, Tanganyika iliwekwa chini ya Uingereza kama eneo la mamlaka ya Shirikisho la Mataifa, na baada ya Vita Kuu ya Pili ya Dunia ikawa eneo la udhamini la Umoja wa Mataifa. Uingereza haikupata umiliki wa Tanganyika kama mali binafsi; ilipewa jukumu la kimataifa, ingawa utawala uliendelea kuwa wa kikoloni. Utawala wa Waingereza ulitumia viongozi wa maeneo katika mfumo unaoitwa utawala usio wa moja kwa moja. Hata hivyo, mamlaka yao yalitegemea na kubadilishwa na utawala wa kikoloni; mfumo huo haukuwa kuacha jamii zitawale bila kuingiliwa.

Zanzibar ilikuwa na historia tofauti. Ilikuwa chini ya usultani wenye uhusiano na Oman kabla ya kuwa eneo la ulinzi la Uingereza mwaka 1890. Katika eneo la ulinzi, sultani aliendelea kuwepo, lakini Uingereza ilikuwa na ushawishi mkubwa katika maamuzi muhimu. Uchumi wa karafuu na historia ya utumwa ulihusisha tofauti kubwa za mamlaka na mali. Kwa hiyo usitumie jina Tanganyika kueleza kila jambo la Zanzibar au kuhamisha tarehe za utawala wa bara kwenda visiwani. Ulinganisho unahitaji kutenganisha taasisi, maeneo na mabadiliko ya kila upande.

Uchumi wa kikoloni ulitegemea kodi, kazi na uzalishaji wa bidhaa za kuuza nje; mahitaji ya wakazi hayakuwa na nafasi sawa na maslahi ya utawala. Elimu na huduma zilitolewa kwa kiwango kisicholingana kati ya maeneo na makundi, na nafasi nyingi za juu zilibaki zimedhibitiwa. Lugha, dini na mafunzo vilienea kupitia serikali, wamisionari na mwingiliano wa watu, lakini Waafrika pia walichagua, walibadili na walipinga. Mahusiano ya leo na mataifa yaliyotawala yanaweza kuhusisha biashara, lugha, elimu na mijadala ya urithi; maelezo ya leo yanahitaji kutaja kipindi na si kuyachukulia kama ukoloni uleule bila uchunguzi.
examples: Mfano wa ulinganisho wa tarehe: Mwanafunzi anaandika Zanzibar ilikuwa eneo la udhamini la Umoja wa Mataifa. Tunatenganisha maeneo: Tanganyika ndiyo ilikuwa eneo la udhamini chini ya Uingereza; Zanzibar ilikuwa eneo la ulinzi hadi uhuru wake mwaka 1963. Kurekebisha jina la eneo hubadilisha pia maelezo ya taasisi.

Mfano wa kutathmini reli: Reli inaweza kusafirisha watu na mazao, lakini katika uchambuzi wa kikoloni tunatafuta njia yake, bidhaa zilizolengwa, chanzo cha fedha na hali ya kazi. Matumizi yenye faida baadaye hayathibitishi kwamba ujenzi ulikuwa wa haki kwa watu wote wakati ule.

Mfano wa utawala usio wa moja kwa moja: Kiongozi wa eneo akikusanya kodi kwa maagizo ya serikali ya kikoloni, kutumia mtu wa eneo hakumaanishi watu wamejipatia uhuru wa maamuzi. Kigezo ni nani ana mamlaka ya mwisho, anayepanga kodi na anayeweza kubadilisha kiongozi.
glossary: Utawala usio wa moja kwa moja
lessons.summary: Ukoloni ni utawala wa nguvu ya kigeni juu ya eneo na watu wake, ukiwapa watawala wa nje uwezo wa kuamua mambo muhimu.

lessons.title: Kupinga utawala wa kikoloni na kulinda utu
objectives: Kueleza sababu na njia tofauti za upinzani.
Kutumia mifano ya Abushiri, Wahehe na Maji Maji kwa mfuatano sahihi.
Kutathmini maadili na athari za upinzani bila kusifu madhara kwa raia.
paragraphs: Kabla ya uvamizi wa kikoloni, jamii zilikuwa na njia mbalimbali za kufundisha wajibu, kusaidiana na kutatua migogoro. Hali hiyo haimaanishi maisha yalikuwa bila vita, utumwa au tofauti za mamlaka. Uvamizi uliingilia taasisi zilizokuwepo na kuanzisha utii kwa mamlaka ya kigeni. Kazi ya kulazimishwa, kodi, unyakuzi wa ardhi na udhibiti wa maamuzi vilisababisha hofu na upinzani. Athari kwa maadili zichunguzwe kwa mifano: kulazimishwa kunaweza kuvunja heshima ya utu, huku kutegemeana katika shida kukiimarisha mshikamano.

Upinzani ulikuwa na njia nyingi: mapigano, kukataa kushirikiana, kuondoka maeneo fulani, maombi ya kisiasa na kudumisha maarifa au desturi. Watu walifanya maamuzi chini ya hali tofauti za nguvu na hatari. Mazungumzo au kukubali mpango fulani havithibitishi moja kwa moja kukosa uzalendo; wakati mwingine vilikuwa mbinu za kuokoa maisha au kupata nafasi ya kuendelea kujipanga. Historia ya upinzani inahitaji kutofautisha nia, hatua, matokeo na mazingira badala ya kuwapa watu wote sifa au lawama moja.

Upinzani wa pwani uliohusishwa na Abushiri mwaka 1888–1889 ulipinga upanuzi wa mamlaka ya Kampuni ya Afrika Mashariki ya Kijerumani na hatua zilizovuruga mamlaka na biashara. Katika maeneo ya Wahehe, mapambano dhidi ya Wajerumani yalihusishwa na uongozi wa Mkwawa; jeshi la Kijerumani lilishindwa Lugalo mwaka 1891. Mapambano yaliendelea baada ya tukio hilo, na Mkwawa alikufa mwaka 1898. Mifano hii inaonyesha tofauti za mazingira na muda; kushinda pambano moja hakumaanishi mwisho wa utawala au wa mapambano yote.

Vita vya Maji Maji vya 1905–1907 vilienea katika sehemu za kusini na maeneo mengine ya Tanganyika ya baadaye. Malalamiko yalihusu utawala wa ukandamizaji, kodi, kazi na masharti ya uzalishaji, yakiwemo mazao ya pamba katika baadhi ya maeneo. Kinjikitile Ngwale alihusishwa na ujumbe wa umoja na maji katika mwanzo wa harakati. Imani ya maji inachunguzwa kama sehemu ya kuhamasisha watu; si uthibitisho kwamba maji yaliweza kuzuia risasi. Ushiriki na sababu havikuwa sawasawa katika kila eneo.

Ukandamizaji wa Wajerumani ulijumuisha kuharibu makazi, mazao na akiba za chakula, na njaa iliongeza vifo na mateso. Matokeo hayo yanakumbusha kwamba gharama za vita huwapata pia raia wasiopigana. Ushujaa wa kupinga kunyimwa uhuru unaweza kuthaminiwa bila kuficha madhara au kutangaza kila mbinu kuwa ya haki. Katika kutathmini uzalendo, tunaangalia kujali watu, kupinga dhuluma, kushirikiana na kutafuta mustakabali wenye heshima, si chuki kwa watu wa leo kutokana na utaifa wao.

Jamii ziliendeleza lugha, malezi, msaada kwa wenye shida, ibada, kazi na sanaa kwa njia zilizobadilika. Kukaa pamoja, kusaidia waliopoteza mali na kufundisha historia kulilinda utambulisho na mshikamano. Hata hivyo, utunzaji wa maadili haukuwa kukataa kila jambo jipya; watu waliweza kuchukua elimu au mbinu mpya na kuzitumia kudai haki. Tunapaswa kuepuka kusema jamii ilipoteza maadili yote au ilihifadhi kila kitu bila mabadiliko. Uaminifu wa historia unahitaji ushahidi wa kilichobadilika, kilichoendelea na sababu zake.
examples: Mfano wa kutenganisha tukio na matokeo: Lugalo 1891 ilikuwa ushindi wa Wahehe katika pambano maalumu. Mwanafunzi akiandika kwamba ukoloni uliisha mwaka huo, anachanganya kiwango cha tukio na mchakato. Tunasahihisha kwa kueleza kwamba mapambano yaliendelea na mamlaka ya Kijerumani baadaye yaliimarishwa.

Mfano wa kusoma imani: Kauli ya kihistoria kuhusu maji inaweza kutuonyesha jinsi ujumbe ulivyojenga matumaini na umoja. Haitumiki kama maelekezo ya kinga ya mwili. Tunatofautisha kazi ya imani katika jamii na uwezo wa kimwili unaohitaji ushahidi wa kisayansi.

Mfano wa tathmini ya maadili: Katika taarifa ya kubuni, jamii inaficha chakula kwa familia zilizopoteza makazi. Hatua hiyo inaonyesha msaada na utu. Ukitathmini kitendo cha kuharibu chakula cha raia, pima matokeo ya njaa na wajibu wa kuwalinda; usitumie upande wa mhusika pekee kuamua haki.
lessons.summary: Kabla ya uvamizi wa kikoloni, jamii zilikuwa na njia mbalimbali za kufundisha wajibu, kusaidiana na kutatua migogoro.

lessons.title: Njia za uhuru wa Tanganyika na Zanzibar na Mapinduzi
objectives: Kuweka matukio ya 1954–1964 kwa mfuatano sahihi.
Kulinganisha harakati za Tanganyika na Zanzibar bila kuchanganya uhuru na Mapinduzi.
Kutathmini ahadi za umoja pamoja na haki na mateso ya raia.
paragraphs: Harakati za uhuru zilijengwa juu ya uzoefu wa ukandamizaji, elimu, vyama, wafanyakazi, wakulima na mawasiliano mapana. Katika Tanganyika, Tanganyika African Association ilikuwa sehemu ya kujenga majadiliano ya haki; TANU iliundwa mwaka 1954 chini ya uongozi wa Julius Nyerere na viongozi wengine. Matawi, mikutano na uhamasishaji vilisaidia kuunganisha madai ya kujitawala kutoka maeneo mbalimbali. Wanawake na vijana walishiriki, ingawa majina yao hayatajwi kwa kiwango sawa katika kila simulizi. Uhuru haukuwa kazi ya mtu mmoja pekee.

TANU ilitumia uhamasishaji wa kisiasa, uchaguzi, mazungumzo na hoja katika taasisi za kimataifa, ikiwemo mfumo wa Umoja wa Mataifa kwa eneo la udhamini. Kiswahili kilisaidia mawasiliano kati ya watu wenye lugha tofauti. Misingi ya umoja ilihitaji kupunguza mgawanyiko wa kikabila, kidini na kieneo, huku watu wakiendelea kuwa na tofauti. Tanganyika ilipata uhuru tarehe 9 Desemba 1961, ikiwa na mfumo wa kifalme wa kikatiba kwa mwaka wa kwanza. Ilikuwa jamhuri tarehe 9 Desemba 1962; tarehe hizo mbili zina maana tofauti.

Zanzibar ilikuwa na harakati na vyama vyake katika mazingira ya usultani, ulinzi wa Uingereza, uchumi wa karafuu na tofauti za kijamii. Afro-Shirazi Party, Zanzibar Nationalist Party na Zanzibar and Pemba People’s Party vilikuwa miongoni mwa vyama muhimu. Mipaka ya majimbo, uwakilishi, ushindani wa vyama na tofauti za mali na hadhi zilichochea mvutano. Usawa wa kura kwa jumla na idadi ya viti si kitu kilekile katika mfumo wa majimbo. Historia hii isigeuzwe kuwa dai kwamba kila mtu wa kundi fulani alikuwa na msimamo mmoja wa kisiasa.

Zanzibar ilipata uhuru tarehe 10 Desemba 1963, ikawa usultani huru. Mapinduzi ya tarehe 12 Januari 1964 yaliuangusha usultani na kuleta serikali ya mapinduzi chini ya uongozi wa Abeid Amani Karume. Hivyo Mapinduzi hayakuwa tarehe ya kumaliza eneo la ulinzi la Uingereza; hilo lilikuwa limekoma wakati wa uhuru. Chimbuko la Mapinduzi lichunguzwe kwa kuunganisha tofauti za kihistoria za mamlaka na mali, malalamiko ya uwakilishi na mvutano wa kisiasa. Maelezo ya tukio moja pekee hayawezi kueleza sababu zote.

Mabadiliko ya serikali yalifuatwa na juhudi za kupanua fursa katika ardhi, elimu, afya na ushiriki wa watu waliokuwa wametengwa. Malengo hayo yalihusishwa na usawa na mshikamano. Wakati huo pia kulikuwa na vurugu, vifo, kupotea kwa mali na uhamaji; idadi na maelezo hutofautiana kati ya vyanzo, hivyo tusibuni takwimu. Kuadhimisha mabadiliko kunapaswa kuambatana na kuheshimu waathirika, kukataa adhabu ya kikundi na kutathmini utekelezaji wa ahadi kwa ushahidi. Umoja unaodumu unahitaji usalama na utu kwa wote.

Tanganyika na Zanzibar ziliungana tarehe 26 Aprili 1964 kuunda Jamhuri ya Muungano. Muungano ulikuwa tukio tofauti na uhuru wa kila upande na Mapinduzi ya Zanzibar. Ni muhimu kusema Tanganyika tunapozungumzia bara kabla ya Muungano, na Tanzania katika muktadha unaofaa baada yake. Kutunza mfuatano huu husaidia kuelewa kwa nini siku za kitaifa zina maudhui tofauti. Harakati, uhuru, jamhuri, Mapinduzi na Muungano ni dhana zinazohusiana lakini kila moja ina taasisi na tarehe zake.
examples: Mfano wa kadi za tarehe: Kadi 9 Desemba 1961 inawekwa kwa uhuru wa Tanganyika, 10 Desemba 1963 kwa uhuru wa Zanzibar, 12 Januari 1964 kwa Mapinduzi, na 26 Aprili 1964 kwa Muungano. Kadi ya 9 Desemba 1962 ni jamhuri ya Tanganyika. Hatua hii huzuia kutumia neno uhuru kwa kila mabadiliko.

Mfano wa mfumo wa majimbo: Katika uchaguzi wa kubuni, chama A kinapata kura nyingi katika jimbo moja na kupoteza kwa tofauti ndogo katika majimbo mawili. Kinaweza kuwa na kura nyingi kwa jumla lakini kiti kimoja tu kati ya vitatu. Mfano unaeleza uwezekano wa mfumo; si takwimu za uchaguzi halisi wa Zanzibar.

Mfano wa maadili: Sherehe ya historia inaeleza fursa mpya za elimu na pia inaweka nafasi ya kukumbuka waathirika wa vurugu. Tathmini hii haifuti mabadiliko wala mateso. Inauliza ushahidi wa fursa zilizopanuka na njia za kulinda haki za watu wote ili mshikamano usijengwe kwa kuficha sehemu ya historia.
lessons.summary: Harakati za uhuru zilijengwa juu ya uzoefu wa ukandamizaji, elimu, vyama, wafanyakazi, wakulima na mawasiliano mapana.

lessons.title: Kujenga Taifa hatua kwa hatua: 1961–1966
objectives: Kuchambua hali ya uchumi na huduma zilizorithiwa wakati wa uhuru.
Kueleza hatua za kisiasa na kijamii za 1961–1966 kwa tarehe sahihi.
Kutathmini mafanikio na changamoto kwa vigezo vya usawa, uwajibikaji na uwezo wa rasilimali.
paragraphs: Tanganyika ilipopata uhuru mwaka 1961, ilirithi uchumi uliotegemea sana kilimo na mauzo ya bidhaa chache nje. Huduma, barabara na nafasi za elimu hazikusambaa kwa usawa, na idadi ya watumishi wenye mafunzo ya juu ilikuwa ndogo. Tatizo halikuwa fedha pekee: walimu, wataalamu wa afya na wasimamizi walihitajika pia. Serikali ilihitaji kuongeza huduma na wakati huohuo kudumisha uzalishaji na mapato. Tathmini ya sera inapaswa kuanzia kwenye hali hii, bila kuitumia kama sababu ya kuondoa wajibu wa viongozi.

Mabadiliko ya kisiasa yalihitaji taasisi mpya na mafunzo ya uraia. Julius Nyerere alikuwa Waziri Mkuu wakati wa uhuru, akajiuzulu nafasi hiyo Januari 1962; Rashidi Kawawa akawa Waziri Mkuu. Tanganyika ilipokuwa jamhuri tarehe 9 Desemba 1962, Nyerere akawa Rais. Kuongeza Waafrika katika utumishi wa umma kulilenga kubadili utegemezi na ubaguzi wa mfumo wa kikoloni, lakini kulihitaji mafunzo na mipango ya kuendeleza kazi. Kubadili watu katika ofisi hakutoshi peke yake; uadilifu, uwezo na uwajibikaji ni vipimo vya taasisi.

Mwaka 1964 ulikuwa na changamoto na mabadiliko makubwa. Uasi wa jeshi Tanganyika Januari 1964 ulihusishwa na malalamiko katika jeshi na ulionyesha umuhimu wa uhusiano kati ya jeshi na mamlaka ya kiraia. Katika upande mwingine, Mapinduzi Zanzibar yalikuwa tukio tofauti la Januari 1964. Muungano wa Tanganyika na Zanzibar ulianzishwa tarehe 26 Aprili 1964, na jina Tanzania likatumika baadaye mwaka huo. Serikali ya Muungano na serikali ya Zanzibar ziliendelea kuwa na majukumu kwa utaratibu wa Muungano; si kila jambo likawa chini ya taasisi moja.

Katiba ya muda ya mwaka 1965 iliweka mfumo wa chama kimoja, TANU kwa upande wa Tanganyika na ASP Zanzibar. Madai ya kuimarisha umoja na kupunguza migawanyiko yalikuwa sehemu ya hoja za mfumo huo. Tathmini yake pia inauliza kuhusu ushindani wa kisiasa, uhuru wa maoni na uwajibikaji. Umoja haupimwi kwa kupungua kwa vyama pekee; unahitaji wananchi kusikilizwa na haki kulindwa. Chama Cha Mapinduzi hakikuwa kimeundwa mwaka 1965; TANU na ASP viliungana kuwa CCM mwaka 1977, nje ya kipindi cha sura hii.

Katika uchumi na jamii, serikali ilijaribu kupanua elimu, afya na uwezo wa uzalishaji pamoja na kujenga watumishi na wataalamu wa ndani. Mpango wa kwanza wa maendeleo wa miaka mitano wa 1964–1969 ulianza ndani ya kipindi hiki na kuendelea baada ya 1966. Uhaba wa fedha, watumishi na vifaa uliweka vikwazo; kupanga shule bila walimu au dawa bila usambazaji hakutoshi. Mjadala kuhusu wajibu wa vijana na elimu ulionekana pia katika mgogoro wa wanafunzi wa chuo kikuu kuhusu masharti ya huduma ya taifa mwaka 1966. Ujenzi wa Taifa ulihusisha kujadili haki, gharama ya elimu na wajibu kwa jamii.

Tanzania iliweka msisitizo katika umoja wa Afrika na kuunga mkono ukombozi wa maeneo yaliyobaki chini ya ukoloni au utawala wa kibaguzi. Tanganyika ilikuwa miongoni mwa waanzilishi wa Umoja wa Nchi Huru za Afrika mwaka 1963 kabla ya Muungano. Mahusiano ya kimataifa yalihitaji kusawazisha misingi ya kisiasa na mahitaji ya rasilimali. Katika kuhitimisha kipindi cha 1961–1966, tusihamishe Azimio la Arusha la 1967 kuingia ndani yake, wala kuita kila sera ya baadaye sera ya wakati wa uhuru. Mafanikio na changamoto zipimwe kwa matokeo halisi, muda na watu waliofikiwa.
examples: Mfano wa upangaji: Halmashauri ya mfano ina fedha za vyumba viwili vya darasa lakini mwalimu mmoja tu. Hatua ni kuhesabu watoto na mahitaji, kupanga ajira/mafunzo na vifaa pamoja na ujenzi. Kipimo cha mafanikio si vyumba pekee, bali wanafunzi wanaopata ufundishaji unaofaa.

Mfano wa kosa la wakati: Insha inasema CCM ilianzisha Azimio la Arusha mwaka 1965. Rekebisha sehemu mbili: Azimio la Arusha lilitangazwa mwaka 1967, na CCM iliundwa mwaka 1977. Katika kipindi cha 1965 kulikuwa na TANU na ASP ndani ya mfumo wa chama kimoja katika maeneo yao.

Mfano wa usomaji wa takwimu: Katika kata ya kubuni, shule zinaongezeka kutoka 4 hadi 6, lakini wanafunzi kutoka 400 hadi 900. Wastani ulikuwa 100 kwa shule, sasa 150. Kuongezeka kwa shule ni hatua, lakini ongezeko la mahitaji ni kubwa zaidi; tunahitaji pia taarifa za madarasa, walimu na usambazaji.

questions.content: A pupil says that filtration can produce pure water from salt water. Explain the error and describe a method that can collect the water.

questions.passage: Read this original passage: The village library opened earlier during examination week. Halima arrived before sunrise, but several seats were already occupied. She chose a desk near the window and placed her notes beside a borrowed dictionary. When her friend asked her to leave for the market, she smiled and pointed to the revision timetable on the wall. After an hour, they compared answers to a science exercise. The passage suggests that preparation matters to Halima, without claiming that she studies every hour of every day.

questions.content: A label says Co and another says CO. Explain why their meanings differ.
questions.answerKey: Co is the element cobalt; CO is carbon monoxide, a compound of carbon and oxygen.
questions.markingGuide: Check letter case and whether one or two elements are represented. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A pure substance has particles containing one nitrogen and three hydrogen atoms. Write its formula and total atoms per molecule.
questions.markingGuide: Use element symbols and a subscript for three hydrogen atoms. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why dissolving salt in water is different from forming a new compound.
questions.answerKey: The components remain a mixture and can be separated physically; a new compound involves chemical joining in a fixed ratio.
questions.markingGuide: Compare mixture formation with chemical combination. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Count atoms of each element in 4CO₂.
questions.answerKey: Four carbon atoms and eight oxygen atoms.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply every formula count by the coefficient. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A learner puts sodium in a group because of the first letter of its name. Explain the error.
questions.answerKey: Periodic-table position is based on atomic structure and atomic number, not alphabetical order.
questions.markingGuide: Do not confuse a table group with a naming convention. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: An atom has 19 protons, 20 neutrons and 19 electrons. Give Z, A and its shell arrangement.
questions.markingGuide: Count protons for Z and add protons and neutrons for A. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A neutral atom has arrangement 2,8,6. State its electron number and period.
questions.markingGuide: Add shell populations and count occupied shells. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A magnesium atom loses two electrons. What are its charge and electron arrangement?
questions.markingGuide: The neutral atom starts with 12 electrons. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Compare chlorine-35 and chlorine-37, both with Z=17.
questions.answerKey: Both have 17 protons; they have 18 and 20 neutrons respectively.
questions.markingGuide: Changing neutrons makes isotopes, not a different element. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A student states that every atom has equal proton and neutron numbers. Give a counterexample.
questions.markingGuide: One valid atom with unequal counts disproves the universal claim. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A 50 N force moves a trolley 8 m in the force direction in 10 s. Find work and average power.
questions.markingGuide: Use W=Fs, then P=W/t. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A foot exerts 300 N on 0.015 m². Find the pressure.
questions.markingGuide: Divide normal force by area in m². 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A machine receives 800 J and delivers 200 J useful work. Find efficiency and non-useful energy transfer.
questions.markingGuide: Useful/input ×100%, then subtract useful from input. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Two pupils push a box in opposite directions with equal 40 N forces. Describe the resultant and what it does not tell you.
questions.answerKey: Resultant is zero; it does not by itself tell whether the box is stationary or moving at constant velocity.
questions.markingGuide: Distinguish force balance from state of motion. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why using a larger supporting area can protect soft ground from a heavy load.
questions.answerKey: The same normal force distributed over a larger area gives lower pressure.
questions.markingGuide: Connect the area change to F/A. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A ray makes 18° with a plane mirror. Calculate incidence and reflection angles.
questions.markingGuide: Subtract 18° from 90°. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A student moves from 1 m to 1.5 m in front of a plane mirror. Find the change in object–image separation.
questions.answerKey: Separation changes from 2 m to 3 m, an increase of 1 m.
questions.markingGuide: Both object and virtual image distances contribute. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why a glass window may both transmit light and reflect some light.
questions.answerKey: Different portions of incident light can be transmitted and reflected at its surfaces.
questions.markingGuide: Do not assume transparent means zero reflection. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A ray enters water exactly along the normal. Does the absence of bending prove its speed stays the same?
questions.answerKey: No. Its speed can change at normal incidence without a direction change.
questions.markingGuide: Separate speed change from bending. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why a mirror image can appear behind an opaque wall-mounted mirror.
questions.answerKey: Reflected rays reach the eye as if originating behind the mirror; the image is virtual.
questions.markingGuide: No physical object or real ray convergence is required behind it. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A plant is supplied with more light but its rate stays unchanged. Give two possible limiting factors.
questions.answerKey: Carbon dioxide availability or temperature; water supply can also limit it.
questions.markingGuide: More light need not overcome a different shortage. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain a connection between stomata and the risk of water loss.
questions.answerKey: Open stomata allow carbon dioxide entry but also permit water vapour to leave.
questions.markingGuide: Show the trade-off between gas exchange and water conservation. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: An iodine result is brown rather than blue-black. What can be concluded, and what cannot?
questions.answerKey: Starch was not detected under the test conditions; this alone does not prove the plant has never photosynthesised.
questions.markingGuide: Distinguish a specific observation from a broad claim. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Design a paper-based comparison to investigate the need for light without doing laboratory work.
questions.answerKey: Compare supplied starch-test observations from otherwise similar leaves with illuminated and covered regions, checking controls and prior starch conditions.
questions.markingGuide: State the changed factor, controls and evidence to compare. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why nitrates and magnesium cannot replace sunlight in photosynthesis.
questions.answerKey: They support plant structure and chlorophyll/protein production but do not supply the light energy used by the process.
questions.markingGuide: Distinguish nutrients from energy input. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A learner describes bile as a protein-digesting enzyme. Correct both parts.
questions.answerKey: Bile is not an enzyme; it emulsifies fats and helps neutralise acid. Proteases digest protein.
questions.markingGuide: Correct the identity and function. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why diarrhoea or damaged intestine can affect nutrition even when food is eaten.
questions.answerKey: Food intake does not guarantee effective absorption of water and nutrients; intestinal function matters.
questions.markingGuide: This is a conceptual answer, not a diagnosis. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Compare the roles of teeth and amylase when eating starchy food.
questions.answerKey: Teeth mechanically break it up; amylase chemically breaks down starch.
questions.markingGuide: Mention increased surface area as a link. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Plan three headings for a report interpreting supplied food-test results.
questions.answerKey: Method/conditions, observations/results, and conclusions with limitations.
questions.markingGuide: Observed colour changes should be distinguished from nutrient conclusions. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Why is a meal rich in energy not necessarily balanced?
questions.answerKey: It may lack adequate protein, vitamins, minerals, fibre or water even if it supplies enough energy.
questions.markingGuide: Adequacy involves different nutrient roles. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Convert 0.454545… into a fraction.
questions.markingGuide: 100x−x=45, so x=45/99=5/11. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Solve −4x ≥ 20.
questions.markingGuide: Reverse the sign when dividing by −4. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Round 0.009965 to three significant figures.
questions.markingGuide: The first significant digit is 9 and the next retained digit rounds up. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Order −3/2, −1.2 and −2 from smallest to largest.
questions.markingGuide: Convert −3/2 to −1.5 or use the number line. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Estimate 49.6/0.248 using convenient rounded values, and explain why it is only an estimate.
questions.answerKey: 50/0.25≈200; rounded inputs differ from the originals.
questions.markingGuide: State the approximations used. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Solve x² + 2x − 15 = 0.
questions.markingGuide: Factor as (x+5)(x−3). 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Solve 2x² − 8 = 0.
questions.markingGuide: First obtain x²=4. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Solve x² − 6x + 2 = 0 by completing the square.
questions.markingGuide: (x−3)²=7. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Simplify (3²)³/3⁴.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply exponents inside the power, then subtract. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Multiply (2 × 10³)(4 × 10⁻⁵) and write standard form.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply coefficients and add powers of ten. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Changanua kazi za maneno katika Asha mdogo anakimbia haraka.
questions.answerKey: Asha ni nomino; mdogo kivumishi; anakimbia kitenzi; haraka kielezi.
questions.markingGuide: Kazi itegemee sentensi iliyotolewa. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Unganisha hoja hizi kwa sababu: Tulisoma maktabani. Darasa lilikuwa na kelele.
questions.answerKey: Tulisoma maktabani kwa sababu darasa lilikuwa na kelele.
questions.markingGuide: Kiunganishi kionyeshe sababu kwa usahihi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Tunga aya ya sentensi tatu yenye kiunganishi na kielezi.
questions.answerKey: Tulipanda miti shuleni. Kisha tuliimwagilia kwa uangalifu. Tulishirikiana kwa sababu tulitaka ikue vizuri.
questions.markingGuide: Pima mpangilio, kiunganishi na kielezi katika muktadha. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Tumia yeye bila kufanya msomaji ashindwe kujua anayerejelewa.
questions.answerKey: Amina amefika. Yeye atatusaidia kupanga vitabu.
questions.markingGuide: Rejea ya kiwakilishi iwe wazi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Hariri: je amina amemwona juma
questions.markingGuide: Kagua herufi kubwa na alama ya swali. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Geuza kuwa wingi: Mti huu uliopandwa jana umeota.
questions.markingGuide: Badili nomino, kionyeshi na kirejeshi kwa usahihi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Geuza kuwa umoja: Vitabu hivi vizuri vimefika.
questions.markingGuide: Vipashio vinavyorejelea nomino vipatane. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Sahihisha na eleza: Watoto hawa amefika mapema.
questions.answerKey: Watoto hawa wamefika mapema; kitenzi kipatane na watoto.
questions.markingGuide: Usibadili maana bila sababu. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Tunga sentensi changamani kuhusu mwanafunzi na kitabu.
questions.markingGuide: Onyesha kishazi tegemezi na upatanisho sahihi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Eleza kwa mfano kwa nini umbo la nomino pekee halionyeshi wingi kila wakati.
questions.answerKey: Nyumba imejengwa / nyumba zimejengwa: nomino hubaki ileile lakini kitenzi hubadilika.
questions.markingGuide: Husisha ushahidi na hitimisho. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: A is at 20°E and B at 50°E. If A has local solar time 08:00, find B’s.
questions.markingGuide: Difference 30° gives 2 hours; B is east and ahead. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why a coordinate written only as 7° is incomplete.
questions.answerKey: It needs identification as latitude/longitude and a north/south or east/west direction, plus the other coordinate to locate a point fully.
questions.markingGuide: A number alone cannot specify a location. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Compare the causes of day/night and seasons.
questions.answerKey: Rotation causes day/night; axial tilt with revolution produces the seasonal cycle.
questions.markingGuide: Do not use Sun-distance change as the main seasonal explanation. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Calculate the ideal local-time difference for 7.5° longitude.
questions.markingGuide: 7.5 × 4 minutes per degree. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Why should an ideal longitude answer not automatically be used as a travel clock time?
questions.answerKey: Actual civil time zones and legal time rules may differ from ideal solar-time calculations.
questions.markingGuide: Identify the model’s limitation. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain how loss of vegetation can connect the biosphere and hydrosphere.
questions.answerKey: Fewer plants can change interception, infiltration and runoff, affecting stream flow and erosion.
questions.markingGuide: Give a process link rather than naming two systems. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Correct: The lithosphere is just another word for the crust.
questions.answerKey: It includes the crust and rigid uppermost mantle.
questions.markingGuide: Distinguish structural boundaries. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Trace one water molecule through three water-cycle stages.
questions.answerKey: It evaporates from a lake, condenses in a cloud and returns as precipitation.
questions.markingGuide: Keep stages in a physically possible sequence. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Compare the inner and outer core by state.
questions.answerKey: Inner core is solid; outer core is liquid.
questions.markingGuide: Do not infer state from temperature alone. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Give an example of a geographical model limitation.
questions.answerKey: A layered model may not use true thickness scale or show variations within each layer.
questions.markingGuide: Explain what information is simplified. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A pupil says all people who take large risks are good entrepreneurs. Evaluate the statement.
questions.answerKey: Good entrepreneurship uses research, planning and affordable tests; large unexamined risks can cause avoidable losses.
questions.markingGuide: Distinguish calculated uncertainty from reckless gambling. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Write two neutral questions to investigate demand for a bicycle repair service.
questions.answerKey: Where do you currently get repairs? What affects your choice of repairer?
questions.markingGuide: Questions should not pressure respondents into praising the idea. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A trader expects 40 sales but can survive only if at least 35 sell. Give one way to test this assumption before a large purchase.
questions.answerKey: Use a small trial or reliable customer orders and compare actual sales with the estimate.
questions.markingGuide: Tie the test to demand uncertainty. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why a one-person business can be quick to decide but vulnerable to illness.
questions.answerKey: One owner can decide without consulting partners, but operations may depend on that person’s time and skills.
questions.markingGuide: Link the same ownership structure to both effects. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Total unit purchase and delivery cost is 1200 and selling price 1450. What remains before other costs?
questions.markingGuide: Do not call this final profit without considering other costs. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Classify harvesting tomatoes, canning them and delivering cans to a shop.
questions.answerKey: Primary, secondary and tertiary production respectively.
questions.markingGuide: State how each activity adds usefulness. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: A loan of 80,000 requires 8 payments of 12,000 plus a 2000 fee. Find total repayment and total finance cost.
questions.markingGuide: Include the fee as well as instalments. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Expected stock is 15+24−19 units. A physical count finds 18. Find expected stock and discrepancy.
questions.answerKey: Expected 20; physical stock is 2 units lower.
questions.markingGuide: Investigate rather than silently inventing a sale. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why credit-funded stock creates both an opportunity and an obligation.
questions.answerKey: Goods can be sold before payment is due, but the supplier still must be paid under the terms.
questions.markingGuide: Consider cash flow and the risk of unsold goods. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Give one possible cooperative benefit and one issue to check.
questions.answerKey: Joint purchasing may reduce costs; members should check fees, obligations and governance.
questions.markingGuide: Do not assume every cooperative guarantees a benefit. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Tathmini dai: Jamii isiyo na mfalme ilikuwa haina siasa.
questions.answerKey: Dai si sahihi; mabaraza ya wazee, mifumo ya ukoo au rika ingeweza kupanga mamlaka na maamuzi.
questions.markingGuide: Tofautisha aina za uongozi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Eleza uhusiano kati ya mazingira na aina za uzalishaji bila kutumia kauli ya watu wote.
questions.answerKey: Upatikanaji wa maji au malisho ungeathiri kilimo au ufugaji, lakini jamii ingeweza kuchanganya shughuli na kubadilika.
questions.markingGuide: Epuka kufunga watu wote katika shughuli moja. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Pendekeza ushahidi wa kuchunguza teknolojia ya chuma ya eneo fulani.
questions.answerKey: Zana, mabaki ya tanuru, muktadha wa uchimbaji na simulizi za mafundi vinaweza kulinganishwa.
questions.markingGuide: Vyanzo mbalimbali viunganishwe bila kuharibu urithi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Eleza manufaa na athari hasi zinazoweza kuandamana na biashara ya mbali.
questions.answerKey: Kubadilishana bidhaa na maarifa kunaweza kunufaisha, lakini unyonyaji na biashara ya watumwa vilileta madhara makubwa katika baadhi ya mahusiano.
questions.markingGuide: Linganisha athari kwa makundi na vipindi tofauti. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Kwa nini usihamishe kitu cha kale kutoka mahali kilipopatikana bila rekodi?
questions.answerKey: Muktadha wake unaweza kutoa ushahidi kuhusu matumizi, uhusiano na kipindi; kuondoa kiholela hupoteza taarifa.
questions.markingGuide: Heshimu utaratibu wa utunzaji na utaalamu. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Panga: Muungano, uhuru wa Tanganyika, TANU, Mapinduzi ya Zanzibar.
questions.answerKey: TANU 1954; uhuru wa Tanganyika 1961; Mapinduzi Januari 1964; Muungano Aprili 1964.
questions.markingGuide: Tarehe na mfuatano viendane. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Linganisha upinzani wa silaha na kuondoka eneo lenye masharti ya kazi.
questions.answerKey: Mbinu hutofautiana lakini zote zinaweza kuonyesha kukataa masharti; ushahidi wa lengo na muktadha unahitajika.
questions.markingGuide: Usihukumu kukubali au kupinga kutokana na vita pekee. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Sahihisha dai: Uhuru wa Zanzibar na Mapinduzi yalikuwa tukio lilelile.
questions.answerKey: Uhuru ulikuwa 10 Desemba 1963; Mapinduzi yalikuwa 12 Januari 1964.
questions.markingGuide: Tofautisha matukio na tarehe. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Eleza kwa nini sera za kodi zinaweza kubadili maisha ya kiuchumi.
questions.answerKey: Zinaweza kuhitaji mapato ya fedha na kuathiri namna watu wanavyotumia kazi, ardhi na uzalishaji.
questions.markingGuide: Husisha sera na maamuzi ya jamii kwa ushahidi. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Pendekeza vyanzo viwili vya kuchunguza tukio la upinzani.
questions.answerKey: Nyaraka za kipindi hicho na simulizi au ushahidi wa maeneo husika, vikilinganishwa kwa muktadha.
questions.markingGuide: Chunguza mtunzi, kusudi na mapungufu ya kila chanzo. Alama 2 kwa jibu na maelezo sahihi; alama 1 kwa uelewa sahihi lakini maelezo pungufu.

questions.content: Rewrite in the negative: Asha has a bicycle.
questions.answerKey: Asha does not have a bicycle.
questions.markingGuide: Use does not + base have. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Correct both verbs: Yesterday he buy a book and readed it.
questions.answerKey: Yesterday he bought a book and read it.
questions.markingGuide: The written past form of read stays read, with different pronunciation. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Write one routine sentence and one sentence about an action happening now.
questions.answerKey: I walk to school every day. I am reading now.
questions.markingGuide: Use simple present for the routine and progressive for the present action. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Explain why an university is incorrect in ordinary English.
questions.answerKey: University begins with a consonant /j/ sound, so a university is used.
questions.markingGuide: Article choice follows sound rather than the written vowel alone. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Give a polite request for directions to a library.
questions.answerKey: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the library?
questions.markingGuide: Use a clear destination and appropriate politeness. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.

questions.content: Give one fact and one inference from the Halima passage, labeling them.
questions.answerKey: Fact: she had a borrowed dictionary. Inference: revision was a priority for her that morning.
questions.markingGuide: Separate stated evidence from a reasoned conclusion. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.
questions.passage: Read this original passage: The village library opened earlier during examination week. Halima arrived before sunrise, but several seats were already occupied. After an hour, they compared answers to a science exercise. The passage suggests that preparation matters to Halima, without claiming that she studies every hour of every day.

questions.content: Evaluate: Halima had never been to a market in her life.
questions.answerKey: Unsupported. Her response on one morning does not establish her lifelong behaviour.
questions.markingGuide: Identify the overgeneralisation. 2 marks for a correct response with required reasoning; 1 for a correct key idea with incomplete reasoning.
questions.passage: Read this original passage: The village library opened earlier during examination week. Halima arrived before sunrise, but several seats were already occupied. After an hour, they compared answers to a science exercise. The passage suggests that preparation matters to Halima, without claiming that she studies every hour of every day.

questions.content:
(a(i)) The gradient of the line ky=kx+x+7 is 2. Find the value of k.

(a(ii)) Write down its y-intercept.

(b) The graph of straight line Kx−My−4=0 passes through the points A(−2,−5) and B(2,−3). Find the values of K and M.

questions.markingGuide: Independent SomaSmart self-assessment rubric (not an official NECTA scheme). (a) Five marks: rearranged slope form; correct gradient equation; solve k=1; identify intercept expression 7/k; obtain intercept 7 (one each). (b) Five marks: substitute A; substitute B; solve M=1; solve K=1/2; verify both points (one each). Accept valid equivalent methods and apply reasonable follow-through without double-penalising one arithmetic slip.
questions.workedSolution: (a) For k≠0, y=((k+1)/k)x+7/k. Set (k+1)/k=2, giving k=1 and intercept 7. k=0 gives a vertical condition rather than the stated finite gradient. (b) −2K+5M=4 and 2K+3M=4; addition gives M=1, then K=1/2. Both source points satisfy the resulting line.

questions.answerKey: (a) y=28.2 cm. (b) A right triangle with vertical side 5 m, horizontal side 12 m and ladder as hypotenuse; ladder=13 m.
questions.markingGuide: Independent SomaSmart self-assessment rubric (not an official NECTA scheme). (a) Five marks: identify opposite side; sine ratio; rearrange to y=30sin70°; correct numerical evaluation; rounding and cm (one each). (b) Five marks: correctly labelled right-triangle sketch; Pythagorean equation; sum 169; square root 13; metres and interpretation of the sketch (one each). Accept valid equivalent methods and apply reasonable follow-through without double-penalising one arithmetic slip.
questions.workedSolution: (a) sin70°=y/30, so y=30sin70°≈28.1908 cm, giving 28.2 cm. (b) Interpreting the ladder as reaching the stated 5 m height, L²=5²+12²=169, so L=13 m. The wall and ground are perpendicular as the stated vertical/ground model requires.

questions.markingGuide: Any three of moisture, heat, pests, theft and contamination. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 3 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Define inventory.
questions.answerKey: Stocks of goods or materials held for sale or business use.
questions.markingGuide: Stocks of goods or materials held for sale or business use. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Name four stock-card fields.
questions.answerKey: Date, reference, receipts, issues and balance; any four.
questions.markingGuide: Date, reference, receipts, issues and balance; any four. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 4 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Opening 40, receipts 25, issues 18: find balance.
questions.markingGuide: 40 + 25 − 18 = 47 units. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Why carry out physical stock counts?
questions.answerKey: To compare actual quantities with recorded balances and investigate differences.
questions.markingGuide: To compare actual quantities with recorded balances and investigate differences. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Give two possible causes of stock differences.
questions.answerKey: Recording errors and damage; accept spoilage or theft.
questions.markingGuide: Recording errors and damage; accept spoilage or theft. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Explain FIFO.
questions.answerKey: Issue earlier-received stock before later receipts.
questions.markingGuide: Issue earlier-received stock before later receipts. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Explain FEFO.
questions.answerKey: Issue stock with the earliest expiry date first.
questions.markingGuide: Issue stock with the earliest expiry date first. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Why can FIFO and FEFO differ?
questions.answerKey: Later deliveries may have earlier expiry dates.
questions.markingGuide: Later deliveries may have earlier expiry dates. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Define lead time.
questions.answerKey: Time between ordering and receiving goods.
questions.markingGuide: Time between ordering and receiving goods. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Calculate reorder point for demand 5/day, lead time 6 days, safety stock 8.
questions.markingGuide: 5 × 6 + 8 = 38 units. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Why can excessive inventory harm a business?
questions.answerKey: It ties up cash and increases storage or deterioration risk.
questions.markingGuide: It ties up cash and increases storage or deterioration risk. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 2 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Name three measures for reviewing an enterprise trial.
questions.answerKey: Profit, cash balance and customer feedback; accept stock loss, repeat purchases or delivery reliability.
questions.markingGuide: Profit, cash balance and customer feedback; accept stock loss, repeat purchases or delivery reliability. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 3 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Prepare a stock card: opening 70, purchase 40, sale 55, damage 4 and sale 20. Include transaction references and investigate a final count of 29.
questions.answerKey: Balances 110, 55, 51, 31; physical count 29 gives shortage 2; separate damage from sales; references and units clear; investigate records/counts before attributing theft.
questions.markingGuide: Balances 110, 55, 51, 31; physical count 29 gives shortage 2; separate damage from sales; references and units clear; investigate records/counts before attributing theft. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 6 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Design a safe storeroom layout for packaged stationery and cleaning products.
questions.answerKey: Separate incompatible stock; secure cleaning products; dry stationery storage; clear aisles; safe stacking; labelled locations and controlled access.
questions.markingGuide: Separate incompatible stock; secure cleaning products; dry stationery storage; clear aisles; safe stacking; labelled locations and controlled access. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 6 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: Plan a one-week enterprise trial based on an observed local need, integrating purchasing, stock and cash records.
questions.answerKey: Document need and customer evidence; limited quantity/budget; supplier and lead time; stock card and cash record; price/cost comparison; end-week review using actual results and limitations.
questions.markingGuide: Document need and customer evidence; limited quantity/budget; supplier and lead time; stock card and cash record; price/cost comparison; end-week review using actual results and limitations. Award one mark for each distinct correct point or correctly explained step, up to 6 marks. Accept equivalent wording and valid alternatives.

questions.content: State two kinds of question studied in chemistry.
questions.answerKey: What substances contain; how they change, or what properties they have.
questions.markingGuide: What substances contain; how they change, or what properties they have.

questions.content: A laboratory measures the amount of iron in water. Name the most directly relevant branch.
questions.markingGuide: Analytical chemistry.

questions.content: Which branch studies enzyme action in cells?
questions.markingGuide: Biochemistry.

questions.content: Why can making a medicine involve both organic chemistry and biology?
questions.answerKey: Organic chemistry investigates the compound and its structure; biology investigates its effects on living systems.
questions.markingGuide: Organic chemistry investigates the compound and its structure; biology investigates its effects on living systems.

questions.content: Give one chemical question and one biological question about a poorly growing maize plant.
questions.answerKey: Chemical: which mineral ions are available in its soil? Biological: are pests or disease damaging the plant?
questions.markingGuide: Chemical: which mineral ions are available in its soil? Biological: are pests or disease damaging the plant?

questions.content: Explain how mathematics supports a comparison of two water samples.
questions.answerKey: It helps calculate amounts per equal volume and compare measurements on the same basis.
questions.markingGuide: It helps calculate amounts per equal volume and compare measurements on the same basis.

questions.content: Separate observation from interpretation: “Bubbles formed, therefore oxygen was produced.”
questions.answerKey: Bubbles formed is an observation. Oxygen identification is an interpretation requiring a suitable gas test.
questions.markingGuide: Bubbles formed is an observation. Oxygen identification is an interpretation requiring a suitable gas test.

questions.content: Name one benefit and one possible environmental cost of fertiliser use.
questions.answerKey: Benefit: replacing mineral nutrients to support crops. Cost: excess nutrients may enter water and promote algal growth.
questions.markingGuide: Benefit: replacing mineral nutrients to support crops. Cost: excess nutrients may enter water and promote algal growth.

questions.content: Why does the word chemical alone not establish whether a substance is safe?
questions.answerKey: Risk depends on the substance, amount, exposure and conditions of use; the label alone supplies none of these.
questions.markingGuide: Risk depends on the substance, amount, exposure and conditions of use; the label alone supplies none of these.

questions.content: Suggest two stages outside product use that should be considered when comparing packaging materials.
questions.answerKey: Raw-material extraction and disposal or recycling; manufacturing energy is also valid.
questions.markingGuide: Raw-material extraction and disposal or recycling; manufacturing energy is also valid.

questions.content: A new process makes twice as much product but consumes three times the water. Explain why output alone cannot decide its suitability.
questions.answerKey: Water use per unit product has risen; local water availability, costs and other effects must also be considered.
questions.markingGuide: Water use per unit product has risen; local water availability, costs and other effects must also be considered.

questions.content: Distinguish organic chemistry from physical chemistry using one example each.
questions.answerKey: Organic: studying carbon compounds such as fuels. Physical: studying energy transfer or reaction rates.
questions.markingGuide: Organic: studying carbon compounds such as fuels. Physical: studying energy transfer or reaction rates.

questions.content: Why may a chemist repeat a measurement before reporting a water-quality result?
questions.answerKey: Repeats reveal variation and help identify unreliable or unusual readings.
questions.markingGuide: Repeats reveal variation and help identify unreliable or unusual readings.

questions.content: A factory releases clearer wastewater after treatment. Has this proved the water is chemically safe? Explain.
questions.answerKey: No. Dissolved or colourless harmful substances may remain and require appropriate testing.
questions.markingGuide: No. Dissolved or colourless harmful substances may remain and require appropriate testing.

questions.content: Give a reason to compare cost per kilogram of useful product rather than total production cost alone.
questions.answerKey: The processes may make different amounts, so cost per kilogram allows a fairer comparison.
questions.markingGuide: The processes may make different amounts, so cost per kilogram allows a fairer comparison.

questions.content: Construct a table for three products used at home or school. For each, record its purpose, one material or substance, a chemistry branch involved and one disposal consideration.
questions.answerKey: Example rows: soap—cleaning—fat-derived compounds—organic chemistry—avoid unnecessary discharge; steel ruler—measurement—iron alloy—inorganic chemistry—reuse or recycle; drinking-water treatment—microbial control—approved disinfectant—analytical chemistry for checking dose—manage residues appropriately.
questions.markingGuide: Award one mark for each of three sensible purpose/material links and one for each of three justified branch or disposal links. Other sound products are acceptable.

questions.content: Design a paper-based comparison of two cooking fuels for a school. State four measurements or evidence sources and explain how each informs the decision.
questions.answerKey: Compare cost per useful heat delivered, smoke or pollutant evidence, availability, and resource or disposal impacts. Equal heating tasks make comparisons more meaningful. Evidence should come from documented data or supervised measurements, not unsupervised burning.
questions.markingGuide: Compare cost per useful heat delivered, smoke or pollutant evidence, availability, and resource or disposal impacts. Equal heating tasks make comparisons more meaningful. Evidence should come from documented data or supervised measurements, not unsupervised burning.

questions.content: Write a short evidence-based recommendation from these supplied data: filter A removes visible particles only; filter B removes particles and a tested dissolved contaminant; B costs more. State what is known and one further question.
questions.answerKey: B addresses the tested contaminant as well as particles, so it may better meet that specific need. Its higher cost must be assessed against the available budget. Ask whether either system also controls pathogens or other local contaminants; the supplied evidence does not establish complete drinking-water safety.
questions.markingGuide: B addresses the tested contaminant as well as particles, so it may better meet that specific need. Its higher cost must be assessed against the available budget. Ask whether either system also controls pathogens or other local contaminants; the supplied evidence does not establish complete drinking-water safety.

questions.content: Classify grinding sugar and explain.
questions.answerKey: Physical: the grains become smaller but remain sugar.
questions.markingGuide: Physical: the grains become smaller but remain sugar.

questions.content: Classify iron rusting and explain.
questions.markingGuide: Chemical: new iron-containing substances form.

questions.content: Why is freezing water a physical change?
questions.answerKey: It changes state while remaining water.
questions.markingGuide: It changes state while remaining water.

questions.content: A student calls all irreversible changes chemical. Give a counterexample.
questions.answerKey: Breaking a glass is difficult to reverse but produces no different chemical substance.
questions.markingGuide: Breaking a glass is difficult to reverse but produces no different chemical substance.

questions.content: Give two observations that may suggest a reaction.
questions.answerKey: Gas formation and a new solid, or a colour change or energy transfer.
questions.markingGuide: Gas formation and a new solid, or a colour change or energy transfer.

questions.content: Why are bubbles insufficient evidence for a chemical change?
questions.answerKey: They can be vapour produced by a physical change such as boiling.
questions.markingGuide: They can be vapour produced by a physical change such as boiling.

questions.content: Distinguish a precipitate formed by reaction from crystals formed by cooling a solution.
questions.answerKey: A precipitate may be a new insoluble reaction product; cooling can separate unchanged dissolved solute as crystals.
questions.markingGuide: A precipitate may be a new insoluble reaction product; cooling can separate unchanged dissolved solute as crystals.

questions.content: A solution is left in a dish and salt crystals remain. Which material mainly left the dish?
questions.markingGuide: The solvent, usually water, evaporated.

questions.content: Explain why melting candle wax and burning candle wax receive different classifications.
questions.answerKey: Melting changes state; burning forms new substances.
questions.markingGuide: Melting changes state; burning forms new substances.

questions.content: Why may the mass of burning magnesium increase although mass is conserved?
questions.answerKey: Oxygen from the surroundings joins magnesium in the product; measuring magnesium alone excludes the entering oxygen.
questions.markingGuide: Oxygen from the surroundings joins magnesium in the product; measuring magnesium alone excludes the entering oxygen.

questions.content: An open reaction flask loses mass as a gas escapes. Does this show atoms were destroyed?
questions.answerKey: No. Matter left the measured system as gas.
questions.markingGuide: No. Matter left the measured system as gas.

questions.content: A closed apparatus initially has 83.4 g of contents. No matter enters or leaves during reaction. Predict its final contents mass.
questions.answerKey: 83.4 g; matter is conserved in the closed system.
questions.markingGuide: 83.4 g; matter is conserved in the closed system.

questions.content: Describe one difference between an iron–sulfur mixture and iron sulfide.
questions.answerKey: Iron in a mixture can retain its magnetic behaviour and be separated physically; chemically combined iron in iron sulfide has different properties and is not separated in the same way.
questions.markingGuide: Iron in a mixture can retain its magnetic behaviour and be separated physically; chemically combined iron in iron sulfide has different properties and is not separated in the same way.

questions.content: State what further evidence is useful when a liquid changes colour after mixing.
questions.answerKey: Compare with controls and test whether a different substance formed; colour change alone may result from dilution or mixing colours.
questions.markingGuide: Compare with controls and test whether a different substance formed; colour change alone may result from dilution or mixing colours.

questions.content: Explain what happens to atoms in an ordinary chemical reaction.
questions.answerKey: Existing atoms rearrange into different combinations; they are conserved rather than created or destroyed.
questions.markingGuide: Existing atoms rearrange into different combinations; they are conserved rather than created or destroyed.

questions.content: Prepare a classification chart for melting ice, crushing chalk, rusting iron, evaporating salt solution, burning fuel and cutting paper. Include a reason for every classification.
questions.answerKey: Physical: melting ice, crushing chalk, evaporating salt solution and cutting paper, because identity is retained. Chemical: rusting iron and burning fuel, because different substances form.
questions.markingGuide: Physical: melting ice, crushing chalk, evaporating salt solution and cutting paper, because identity is retained. Chemical: rusting iron and burning fuel, because different substances form.

questions.content: Interpret this supplied investigation: a sealed flask and contents weigh 120.2 g before and after a gas-producing reaction. When the flask is opened, the measured mass falls to 119.7 g. Calculate the mass that escaped and explain both observations.
questions.answerKey: 120.2 − 119.7 = 0.5 g escaped. While sealed, all products were retained, so total mass stayed constant. Opening let gas leave the measured system.
questions.markingGuide: 120.2 − 119.7 = 0.5 g escaped. While sealed, all products were retained, so total mass stayed constant. Opening let gas leave the measured system.

questions.content: Write a claim–evidence–reasoning paragraph for this observation: a solid appears when a clear salt solution cools; reheating dissolves it again. Do not claim more than the evidence supports.
questions.answerKey: Claim: crystallisation is a likely physical explanation. Evidence: solid appears on cooling and dissolves on reheating. Reasoning: solubility often falls on cooling, so unchanged solute separates; identification of the solid would strengthen the conclusion.
questions.markingGuide: Claim: crystallisation is a likely physical explanation. Evidence: solid appears on cooling and dissolves on reheating. Reasoning: solubility often falls on cooling, so unchanged solute separates; identification of the solid would strengthen the conclusion.

questions.content: Name the usual horizontal-axis quantity on a heating graph.
questions.markingGuide: Time.

questions.content: Why should a thermometer bulb not rest on the heated vessel base?
questions.answerKey: It may measure the base temperature rather than represent the sample temperature.
questions.markingGuide: It may measure the base temperature rather than represent the sample temperature.

questions.content: Explain why temperature may stay steady while a pure solid melts.
questions.answerKey: Energy changes particle arrangement during melting rather than increasing average particle motion.
questions.markingGuide: Energy changes particle arrangement during melting rather than increasing average particle motion.

questions.content: State two conditions to keep similar when comparing heating of equal samples.
questions.answerKey: Heating power and sample mass; vessel type and initial temperature are also suitable.
questions.markingGuide: Heating power and sample mass; vessel type and initial temperature are also suitable.

questions.content: Distinguish evaporation from boiling by location in the liquid.
questions.answerKey: Evaporation occurs at the surface; boiling occurs throughout the liquid.
questions.markingGuide: Evaporation occurs at the surface; boiling occurs throughout the liquid.

questions.content: A sample warms from 18 °C to 42 °C. Calculate the temperature increase.
A sample warms by 30 °C in 5 minutes. Find its mean temperature rise per minute.
questions.markingGuide: 30/5 = 6 °C per minute.

questions.content: Does a plateau on its own prove a substance is pure? Explain.
questions.answerKey: No. Apparatus or measurement conditions can also produce near-steady readings; observations and further evidence are needed.
questions.markingGuide: No. Apparatus or measurement conditions can also produce near-steady readings; observations and further evidence are needed.

questions.content: What happens to particles when water freezes?
questions.answerKey: They adopt the solid arrangement and have less freedom to move; they are not destroyed.
questions.markingGuide: They adopt the solid arrangement and have less freedom to move; they are not destroyed.

questions.content: Why should a hot vessel be treated as hazardous after heating stops?
questions.answerKey: It can retain enough thermal energy to cause burns.
questions.markingGuide: It can retain enough thermal energy to cause burns.

questions.content: State a safe rule about heating a sealed container.
questions.answerKey: Do not heat it; pressure can build and rupture the container.
questions.markingGuide: Do not heat it; pressure can build and rupture the container.

questions.content: Why may a real melting interval not be perfectly horizontal?
questions.answerKey: Impurities, uneven heating, heat loss or measurement limits can affect the readings.
questions.markingGuide: Impurities, uneven heating, heat loss or measurement limits can affect the readings.

questions.content: Explain condensation on a cold window.
questions.answerKey: Water vapour in air loses energy near the cold surface and changes into liquid droplets.
questions.markingGuide: Water vapour in air loses energy near the cold surface and changes into liquid droplets.

questions.content: Name one observation to record besides temperature during melting.
questions.answerKey: Whether solid, liquid, or both are visible.
questions.markingGuide: Whether solid, liquid, or both are visible.

questions.content: Why should an unexpected reading be retained with a note rather than silently replaced?
questions.answerKey: It is part of the evidence; changing it would hide uncertainty or possible experimental error.
questions.markingGuide: It is part of the evidence; changing it would hide uncertainty or possible experimental error.

questions.content: Plot a heating graph from these supplied time/minute and temperature/°C pairs: (0,20), (1,35), (2,50), (3,50), (4,50), (5,65). Label axes and identify a likely state-change interval.
questions.answerKey: Time belongs on the horizontal axis and temperature on the vertical. Plot all six points. A plateau from 2 to 4 minutes at 50 °C may indicate a state change if supported by observations.
questions.markingGuide: Time belongs on the horizontal axis and temperature on the vertical. Plot all six points. A plateau from 2 to 4 minutes at 50 °C may indicate a state change if supported by observations.

questions.content: Design a supervised comparison of cooling water in an insulated cup and an uninsulated cup. State a prediction, measurements, three controls and one limitation.
questions.answerKey: Prediction: insulation reduces the temperature drop. Record temperature at equal times. Match water volume, initial temperature and cup dimensions or surrounding conditions. A limitation is heat loss through the open top or imperfectly matched cups. Teacher manages hot water.
questions.markingGuide: Prediction: insulation reduces the temperature drop. Record temperature at equal times. Match water volume, initial temperature and cup dimensions or surrounding conditions. A limitation is heat loss through the open top or imperfectly matched cups. Teacher manages hot water.

questions.content: Write a results paragraph for a sample that contains solid and liquid at 72 °C for three readings but rises to 78 °C after the solid disappears. Separate evidence, explanation and uncertainty.
questions.answerKey: Evidence: three readings near 72 °C with both phases, followed by 78 °C when fully liquid. Explanation: melting occurred near 72 °C, using transferred energy for the change of state. Uncertainty: thermometer resolution and sample purity limit the precision of the melting-temperature estimate.
questions.markingGuide: Evidence: three readings near 72 °C with both phases, followed by 78 °C when fully liquid. Explanation: melting occurred near 72 °C, using transferred energy for the change of state. Uncertainty: thermometer resolution and sample purity limit the precision of the melting-temperature estimate.

questions.content: Name Na₂O.
questions.markingGuide: Sodium oxide.

questions.content: Write the formula of calcium sulfide from Ca²⁺ and S²⁻.
questions.answerKey: CaS; +2 and −2 cancel in a 1:1 ratio.
questions.markingGuide: CaS; +2 and −2 cancel in a 1:1 ratio.

questions.content: Write the formula of magnesium chloride.
questions.markingGuide: MgCl₂.

questions.content: Write the formula of aluminium nitride from Al³⁺ and N³⁻.
questions.markingGuide: AlN.

questions.content: Explain the Roman numeral in iron(III) oxide.
questions.answerKey: It indicates iron has oxidation state +3, not that the compound contains three iron atoms.
questions.markingGuide: It indicates iron has oxidation state +3, not that the compound contains three iron atoms.

questions.content: Derive the formula of iron(III) oxide from Fe³⁺ and O²⁻.
Name CuCl when chloride is Cl⁻.
questions.markingGuide: Copper(I) chloride.

questions.content: State the oxidation state of oxygen in O₂.
questions.answerKey: Zero, because O₂ is an uncombined element.
questions.markingGuide: Zero, because O₂ is an uncombined element.

questions.content: Explain why calcium hydroxide is not a binary compound.
questions.answerKey: It contains three elements: calcium, oxygen and hydrogen.
questions.markingGuide: It contains three elements: calcium, oxygen and hydrogen.

questions.content: Write the formula of sodium carbonate from Na⁺ and CO₃²⁻.
questions.markingGuide: Na₂CO₃.

questions.content: Write the formula of magnesium nitrate.
questions.markingGuide: Mg(NO₃)₂.

questions.content: Count oxygen atoms in Al₂(SO₄)₃.
questions.markingGuide: 3 × 4 = 12 oxygen atoms per formula unit.

questions.content: Distinguish sulfate from sulfide.
questions.answerKey: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻, containing sulfur and oxygen; sulfide is S²⁻.
questions.markingGuide: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻, containing sulfur and oxygen; sulfide is S²⁻.

questions.content: Why is Ca₂O₂ simplified to CaO for calcium oxide?
questions.answerKey: The empirical ionic formula uses the simplest whole-number ion ratio, here 1:1.
questions.markingGuide: The empirical ionic formula uses the simplest whole-number ion ratio, here 1:1.

questions.content: Use charge balance to explain why MgOH is not the correct formula of magnesium hydroxide.
questions.answerKey: Mg²⁺ needs two OH⁻ ions to cancel +2; the formula is Mg(OH)₂.
questions.markingGuide: Mg²⁺ needs two OH⁻ ions to cancel +2; the formula is Mg(OH)₂.

questions.content: Make a charge-balance table for AlCl₃, MgO, Ca₃N₂ and (NH₄)₂CO₃. Show the charge contribution from each kind of ion.
questions.answerKey: AlCl₃: +3 and 3(−1); MgO: +2 and −2; Ca₃N₂: 3(+2) and 2(−3); (NH₄)₂CO₃: 2(+1) and −2. Each total is zero.
questions.markingGuide: AlCl₃: +3 and 3(−1); MgO: +2 and −2; Ca₃N₂: 3(+2) and 2(−3); (NH₄)₂CO₃: 2(+1) and −2. Each total is zero.

questions.content: Correct these proposed formulae and explain the errors: CaNO₃, AlO and NaSO₄.
questions.answerKey: Ca(NO₃)₂ balances Ca²⁺ with two nitrates; Al₂O₃ balances +6 with −6; Na₂SO₄ balances two Na⁺ with sulfate. The proposed formulae did not have zero overall charge.
questions.markingGuide: Ca(NO₃)₂ balances Ca²⁺ with two nitrates; Al₂O₃ balances +6 with −6; Na₂SO₄ balances two Na⁺ with sulfate. The proposed formulae did not have zero overall charge.

questions.content: Build a labelled atom-count inventory for three formula units of Ca(NO₃)₂. Then explain the difference between the coefficient 3 and the subscript 2.
questions.answerKey: Three formula units contain Ca = 3, N = 6, O = 18. The coefficient multiplies the entire formula; the subscript 2 multiplies only the nitrate group in brackets.
questions.markingGuide: Three formula units contain Ca = 3, N = 6, O = 18. The coefficient multiplies the entire formula; the subscript 2 multiplies only the nitrate group in brackets.

questions.content: Why must elemental masses be divided by relative atomic masses?
questions.answerKey: Equal masses of different elements generally contain different numbers of atoms.
questions.markingGuide: Equal masses of different elements generally contain different numbers of atoms.

questions.content: Using C = 12 and O = 16, find the empirical formula from 12 g C and 32 g O.
Using H = 1 and O = 16, find the empirical formula from 2 g H and 16 g O.
Simplify the atomic ratio C:H:O = 2:4:2.
questions.markingGuide: 1:2:1, giving CH₂O.

questions.content: Convert the ratio N:O = 1:1.5 to an empirical formula.
questions.answerKey: Multiply both by 2 to get 2:3; N₂O₃.
questions.markingGuide: Multiply both by 2 to get 2:3; N₂O₃.

questions.content: Calculate the empirical formula mass of CH₂O using C = 12, H = 1 and O = 16.
A compound has empirical formula CH₂ and relative molecular mass 56. Find its molecular formula. Use C = 12, H = 1.
questions.markingGuide: Empirical mass = 14; 56/14 = 4; C₄H₈.
